observations.title: Publication of Website and Third-Party Video Content Without Documented Consent
observations.description:
Publication of Website and Third-Party Video Content Without Documented Consent

We observed control weaknesses in the consent management process for identifiable individuals featured on the Corporation�s website and social media platforms contravening the requirements of the NDPA 2023.

Specifically:

1. Video recordings (street confessions) of individuals outside the organisation were captured and published on digital platforms without documented or signed consent from the individuals concerned.

2. Certain individuals featured on the Corporation�s corporate website do not have documented consent forms authorizing the use of their images or personal information. There was no evidence of a standardized consent acquisition process prior to publication.

3. We also noted that a video recording (Abdulgafar Ismail, a fonemart manager) published by the Corporation to its LinkedIn page in January 2026 was not backed by a signed consent. We noted that this video was not recorded by Credicorp, but by a partner vendor.
observations.risk:
Risk of legal claims relating to privacy, image rights, and data protection.

Exposure to regulatory sanctions under applicable data protection laws.

Reputational damage arising from public complaints or disputes.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: There is no formalised process or control with the social media vendor (Sustainalytics) requiring the execution, retention, and verification of consent forms prior to the recording and publication of content involving external individuals.

No framework guiding the use of third-party personal information in the Corporation.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and enforce a mandatory consent management framework for all recordings involving external individuals.

Introduce standardised written and/or digital consent forms aligned with data protection requirements.

Introduce a pre-publication compliance checklist covering consent, privacy, and legal review.
observations.managementResponse:
1. Currently all posting has been suspended. Secondly a consent form document has been shared with our partner Sustainalytics for subsequent recordings. When we have enough content back up around street confessions, we can start pulling down the old ones without consent.

2. This observation has been noted. As an immediate corrective measure, the affected images will be removed from the corporate website. They will subsequently be replaced with content from the Humans of CREDICORP series.

3. This observation has been noted. Although the referenced video was recorded by a partner vendor and not directly by the Corporation, we recognize the importance of ensuring that all published content complies with the Corporation�s consent documentation requirements.
Accordingly, the CREDICORP consent form will be shared with the partner organization, and follow-up will be conducted to obtain retroactive documentation from the featured individual. Going forward, all partner-generated content intended for publication on the Corporation�s platforms will be required to comply with the Corporation�s consent documentation standards prior to dissemination.

observations.title: Absence of Documented Strategy and Governance Framework for Video Content Series
observations.description:
Absence of Documented Strategy and Governance Framework for Video Content Series
The audit observed that the organisation operates an ongoing video content series published across its digital platforms; however, there is no documented concept note, content strategy, branding guideline, or governance framework guiding its development and dissemination. There was no evidence of defined approval workflows or editorial oversight. This creates ambiguity in accountability, messaging consistency, and risk management.
observations.risk:
Inconsistent messaging and potential misalignment with corporate strategy.

Risk of publishing material that may conflict with institutional values or regulatory expectations.

RATING: LOW
observations.rootCause: Process/Governance: Management has not established formal policies or documentation governing the planning, branding, approval, and oversight of digital content initiatives.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and document a formal concept note outlining objectives, target audience, messaging themes, and alignment with corporate strategy.

Develop a comprehensive external communications policy covering: Content strategy and editorial standards, branding and tone-of-voice guidelines, legal and compliance review requirements, escalation procedures for sensitive content.
observations.managementResponse:
The observation is well noted. While the video content series currently published across the Corporation�s digital platforms has been executed to support public education and stakeholder engagement objectives, it is acknowledged that a formally documented governance framework will strengthen clarity, accountability, and risk management.
To address this, a comprehensive framework will be developed to guide the series, including a documented concept note, defined content strategy, branding alignment guidelines, editorial standards, and structured approval workflows. This framework will also establish clear oversight mechanisms to ensure consistency of messaging and appropriate governance across all digital publications.

observations.title: Non-Compliance with Statutory Corporate Disclosure Requirements
observations.description:
Non-Compliance with Statutory Corporate Disclosure Requirements
We observed that the following has not been disclosed as per the requirements of CAMA 2020:

1. RC number not consistently displayed on all business letters, notices and official publications. Additionally, the company�s name is not prominently displayed at its registered office and other business locations - S. 729 (a) & (c), CAMA 2020

2. Names or initials of directors not consistently displayed on business letters - S. 304 (1), CAMA 2020
observations.risk:
Exposure to regulatory sanctions and fines.

Weak corporate governance and compliance posture.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: People: Limited awareness of mandatory disclosure requirements under applicable company law.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately update all official templates (letters, notices, publications, email signatures, website footer) to include the company�s RC number & director details.

Ensure the company�s name is prominently displayed at the registered office and all operational locations in compliance with statutory requirements.
observations.managementResponse:
This observation has been noted. The current letterhead and corporate stationery design predate my appointment to the role.
However, in order to ensure full compliance with the provisions of CAMA 2020�specifically regarding the display of the Corporation�s RC number and the names or initials of directors�I will engage the Chief of Staff for guidance on the appropriate process for updating the official design templates.
Subject to the necessary approvals, a revised version of the Corporation�s letterhead and related communication templates will be developed to ensure that all statutory disclosure requirements are properly captured across official publications and correspondence.

observations.title: Weak Website Governance and Absence of Data Privacy Disclosure
observations.description:
Weak Website Governance and Absence of Data Privacy Disclosure
Review of the Corporation�s website and related online forms revealed the absence of a published Privacy Notice outlining how personal data collected through the website (e.g., contact forms, subscriptions, enquiries) is processed and protected. Similarly, PFI and vendor onboarding forms do not contain privacy notices informing data subjects of how their information will be used. 

In addition, we observed that the PFI listing on the website is incomplete and that there is no documented process for ensuring timely and complete publication of stakeholder information.
observations.risk:
This creates exposure to data protection non-compliance, transparency gaps, and reputational risk. Stakeholders may be unable to rely on the accuracy and completeness of publicly disclosed institutional information.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process & Governance: Absence of a formal website governance, disclosure management, and data privacy compliance framework.
observations.recommendation:
Publish a Privacy Notice and Data Protection Policy on the website. 

A cookies notice should be put up on all our public facing websites

Update online forms (PFI and vendor onboarding) to include privacy notices and consent language.

Corporate Comms team to conduct a review of all website forms and digital touchpoints to ensure alignment with data protection requirements.

Establish a formal data protection and digital compliance framework.
observations.managementResponse:
1. Privacy Notice & Data Protection Policy
In progress. Legal is currently refreshing the existing policy; once finalized it will be published on the website. 
Target completion: 13 March.

2. Cookies Notice
Not currently applicable as our websites do not deploy cookies or user tracking. A notice will be prepared and implemented if this functionality is introduced.

3. Privacy Notice on Online Forms
Noted. This will be shared with the relevant technology/vendor teams to incorporate appropriate privacy notice and consent language on the forms.

observations.title: Lack of Contractual Safeguards Over Corporate Social Media Administration
observations.description:
Lack of Contractual Safeguards Over Corporate Social Media Administration
We observed that a consultant serves as administrator of the institution�s corporate social media accounts; however, this role is not captured in the contract. The contract also does not provide for transfer of administrative rights upon termination. This creates a risk of loss of control over corporate digital assets and reputational exposure.
observations.risk:
Risk of loss of access to corporate social media accounts if the consultant disengages.

Potential reputational damage due to unauthorized or delayed content management.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Governance: No contractual or policy requirement to safeguard administrative rights upon termination of engagement.

Process: Absence of formal process to govern third-party access and control of corporate digital assets.
observations.recommendation:
Document and formalize the consultant�s role regarding social media administration.

Secure internal super-admin access to all accounts and verify credentials.

Update the contract to include terms on administrative rights and handover on termination.

Develop a social media governance process covering: 
Third-party account administration, credential custody, transfer of rights on contract termination, pre-publication approval workflow.

Ensure dual control where internal staff retain ultimate administrative access.
observations.managementResponse:
This observation has been duly noted. To mitigate the risk identified, the Corporate Communications function will engage with the Administration and Legal teams to review the existing contractual arrangement with the consultant responsible for social media administration.
The review will seek to ensure that the scope of responsibility for social media account administration is formally captured within the contract, including provisions governing ownership of accounts, administrative access rights, and the mandatory transfer of administrative privileges to the Corporation upon termination of the engagement.
This will help ensure continued institutional control over the Corporation�s digital assets and minimize reputational or operational risks.

observations.title: Inaccurate and Inconsistent External Reporting of Disbursement and Impact Metrics
observations.description:
Inaccurate and Inconsistent External Reporting of Disbursement and Impact Metrics
a. We noted that the 2025 recap report cites a disbursement of ?37 billion to 200,224 beneficiaries; however, our assessment indicates that only ?26 billion was disbursed in 2025, with a cumulative total (2024 + 2025) of ?37.9 billion. 

b. Additionally, the impact figures communicated on the website and social media are inconsistent with the recap report. No measurement date/period is specified on the impact metrics displayed on the website. 

These discrepancies create a misleading representation of the Corporation�s performance and impact.
observations.risk:
Misrepresentation of annual disbursement and impact metrics, leading to stakeholder misinformation and reduced confidence in credibility of the Corporation's reports & communications.

Reputational risk arising from inconsistent public reporting.

Potential regulatory scrutiny for inaccurate reporting of corporate operations.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Lack of a standardized reporting and verification process for external communications of disbursement and impact data.
observations.recommendation:
Reconcile internal disbursement records with public reports to correct and clarify discrepancies.

Implement a standardized process for verifying financial and operational metrics prior to publication.

Include clear measurement periods and definitions for all impact and disbursement data on all platforms.
observations.managementResponse: As earlier communicated during the virtual meeting, I may not be in the best position to provide a definitive response to this observation, as my role in this context has primarily been limited to the execution and dissemination of approved communication materials.

observations.title: Incomplete SOP and Unclear Approval Authority for External Communications Processes
observations.description:
Incomplete SOP and Unclear Approval Authority for External Communications Processes
We noted that the process flow for the External Communications unit is not clearly defined in the SOP. Specifically, approval authority for social media content, publication, and dissemination of official materials is not clearly spelt out, and governance steps within the team are ambiguous. This lack of clarity increases the risk of unauthorized or inconsistent communications and reduces accountability within the department.
observations.risk:
Increased risk of unauthorized or inconsistent content being published.

Weak accountability and control over approval processes.

Potential reputational risk if inaccurate or unapproved content is disseminated.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause: Process: SOP does not clearly define all approval steps and authority levels for content publication.
observations.recommendation: Update the SOP to clearly define all external communications processes, including but not limited to content submission, approval hierarchy, governance and control steps, escalation for exceptions or sensitive content.
observations.managementResponse:
This observation has been noted. A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the External Communications function has already been developed to provide structure for the unit�s activities.

However, further refinement is currently underway to ensure that all governance considerations identified�including clearly defined approval authorities for social media publications, official materials, and dissemination processes�are comprehensively captured and standardized.

Upon completion, the updated SOP will provide clearer process flows, defined approval hierarchies, and strengthened accountability mechanisms for all external communication outputs of the Corporation. 
This has a target remediation date of 31 March 2026.

observations.title: Control Gaps in Credit Bureau Due Diligence and Data Governance Framework
observations.description:
Control Gaps in Credit Bureau Due Diligence and Data Governance Framework
We observed weaknesses in the governance, completeness, and control framework surrounding the use of credit bureau reports for PFI onboarding and monitoring.

Specifically:
1. Absence of formal contractual safeguards: Credit bureau checks are conducted through a third-party provider without a signed NDA or formal service agreement. Therefore, customer personal data is shared without documented data protection obligations, liability clauses, or confidentiality safeguards.

2. Incomplete credit bureau coverage for key management personnel: Credit bureau reports were not obtained for all key management staff for certain PFIs, creating gaps in counterparty risk assessment.
observations.risk:
These weaknesses collectively expose the institution to:

- Counterparty credit risk
- Regulatory non-compliance (data privacy and third-party risk management)
- Reputational damage
- Legal liability arising from improper data handling

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Inadequate formalization of the credit bureau due diligence process during the institution�s early operational phase, resulting in gaps in contractual safeguards, completeness requirements, and escalation protocols.
observations.recommendation:
Execute a formal service agreement and NDA/Data Processing Agreement with the credit bureau provider, incorporating confidentiality, data protection, and liability clauses.

Implement a standardized due diligence checklist requiring documented review and sign-off before onboarding decisions.

Define clear escalation thresholds for adverse credit findings, with documented resolution and approval by appropriate authority.
observations.managementResponse:
An NDA has now been executed with the third-party credit bureau provider to formalize confidentiality and data protection obligations.

Additionally, Management has budgeted to procure a dedicated credit reporting bureau service directly for the Corporation going forward, ensuring internal control over data access and enhanced data protection compliance.

Going forward, credit bureau checks on directors and key management of PFIs will be conducted prior to onboarding once the Corporation�s dedicated credit bureau service is fully procured and operational, and periodic reviews will be incorporated into the due diligence process.

observations.title: Deficiencies in Collateral Policy Design and Enforcement for Tier 2 Banks and MFBs
observations.description:
Deficiencies in Collateral Policy Design and Enforcement for Tier 2 Banks and MFBs
We observed weaknesses in the design, clarity, and enforcement of collateral requirements for loans granted to Tier 2 commercial banks and Microfinance Banks (MFBs).

1. Non-Compliance with Existing Collateral Requirements: For certain PFIs (e.g., Optimus Bank), only a Direct Debit Mandate (DDM) was obtained as collateral, contrary to internal policy requiring a combination of collateral types.

2. Ambiguity in Collateral Policy Framework: The credit policy for Tier 2 banks does not specify how multiple collateral types should be combined or how to assess their sufficiency. For example, in a case where a PFI has both a Direct Debit Mandate (DDM) and T-bills, there is no guidance on whether the T-bills adequately cover the exposure or how to combine with other collaterals. This ambiguity increases the risk of under-collateralized loans and inconsistent application of credit risk mitigation.
observations.risk:
The combined weaknesses expose the institution to:

- Under-collateralized loan exposures
- Increased credit loss risk upon default
- Inconsistent credit decision-making
- Weak governance oversight over risk mitigation
- Non-compliance with internal policy requirements

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Policy lacks clear methodology for combining and assessing multiple forms of collateral.

Governance: No framework exists to approve or validate sufficiency of collateral combinations for Tier 2 banks.
observations.recommendation:
Revise the credit policy to provide clear guidance on combining multiple collateral types and assessing sufficiency for Tier 2 banks.

Review all PFI loans assess whether collateral coverage is sufficient relative to exposure and obtain additional collateral where feasible.

A collaterals/securities register should be created (legal to monitor to check enforceability) to drive adequate monitoring, and implement system controls or checklists to ensure multiple collateral types are obtained as required.

Develop a collateral adequacy calculation methodology or scoring system.
observations.managementResponse:
Credit Operations Department will develop and issue a Collateral Management Policy to provide clearer guidance on:

The methodology for assessing collateral adequacy.

Treatment and combination of multiple collateral types (e.g., DDM, Treasury Bills, guarantees).

Management will continue to ensure that all approved collateral structures are clearly documented in credit memos and monitored through the existing collateral register.

observations.title: Deficiencies in Legal Documentation Execution and Quality Control for Financing Agreements
observations.description:
Deficiencies in Legal Documentation Execution and Quality Control for Financing Agreements
We observed weaknesses in the execution control and quality assurance processes over Supplementary Financing Agreements (SFAs).

Specifically:
1. Incomplete Execution of Legal Agreements: We observed several Supplementary Financing Agreements that were unsigned. In some instances, the agreements were executed by the PFIs but not countersigned by the Corporation. 

2. Inconsistencies in Contractual Amounts: We observed instances where the amounts stated in words differ from the amounts stated in figures in certain Supplementary Financing Agreements (SFAs).
observations.risk:
The absence of fully executed agreements and ambiguity/inconsistencies creates significant legal uncertainty regarding enforceability of loan terms and recovery rights.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Inadequate control to ensure agreements are fully executed before loan activation or disbursement, Inadequate document review and quality assurance prior to execution.

People: Lack of accountability for tracking execution status and accuracy of legal documentation.
observations.recommendation:
Conduct a comprehensive review of all active loan files to confirm existence of fully executed agreements, ensuring all outstanding agreements are duly countersigned and properly archived.

Reviewing all executed SFAs to identify discrepancies in contractual amounts and executing corrective addenda or re-executions where required.

Establishing a centralized legal documentation register/tracker with defined ownership and status monitoring.

Institute dual review (Legal and Credit) prior to execution of all financing agreements.
observations.managementResponse:
All affected Master Financing Agreements and Supplementary Financing Agreements have now been fully countersigned and shared with Audit and Legal for proper record-keeping.

Management will continue to ensure that no disbursement is made unless the relevant agreements have been duly executed by all parties.

The isolated instance identified has been corrected. The affected Supplementary Financing Agreement (SFA) was re-executed to eliminate the inconsistency, and the corrected version has been attached and shared with Audit and Legal for proper record-keeping.

Going forward, all SFAs are subject to Legal review prior to execution to ensure document accuracy and consistency.

observations.title: Absence of Portfolio-Level Stress Testing Increasing Risk of Unassessed Credit Vulnerability
observations.description:
Absence of Portfolio-Level Stress Testing Increasing Risk of Unassessed Credit Vulnerability
We observed that portfolio-level stress testing is not conducted, despite the institution�s exposure to concentration and counterparty risk. There is no documented assessment of the impact of adverse scenarios (e.g., PFI default, liquidity stress, economic downturn) on the loan portfolio. This limits management�s ability to proactively assess capital adequacy and risk resilience.
observations.risk:
Inability to quantify potential losses under adverse conditions.

Increased vulnerability to concentration shocks or systemic stress events.

Weak forward-looking risk management and planning capability.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause:
Process: No formal framework for conducting periodic portfolio stress testing.
People: Limited resources or ownership assigned for risk modelling and scenario analysis.
observations.recommendation:
Conduct an initial portfolio stress test covering key scenarios such as default of top PFIs, collateral value haircut, and delayed repayments.

Develop and implement a formal stress testing framework aligned with the institution�s risk profile.
observations.managementResponse: Portfolio-level stress testing will be incorporated into the risk oversight framework as the Risk Management Department begins leveraging the reporting capabilities of the newly functioning banking system to generate structured portfolio analytics.

observations.title: Misalignment Between Supplementary Financing Agreements and Actual Disbursements, Including Disbursement Above Approved Limits
observations.description:
Misalignment Between Supplementary Financing Agreements and Actual Disbursements, Including Disbursement Above Approved Limits
The policy requires that a Supplementary Financing Agreement (SFA) be created per disbursement; however, instances were observed where SFA amounts did not align with actual disbursements. (For example, SLA approved for N1 billion, where disbursement was made in 2 tranches of N500m each) 

In addition, we observed a loan disbursed without accompanying SFA. This represents a weakness in disbursement controls.
observations.risk:
Unauthorized increase in credit exposure beyond approved contractual limits.

Elevated credit and legal risk due to exposure not properly documented or approved.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Absence of reconciliation control between approved SFA amount and disbursement execution.
System: No system restriction preventing disbursement above approved contractual limits.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately investigate the instance where disbursement exceeded the approved SFA amount.

Execute an amended SFA or obtain proper retrospective approval where justified.

Introduce a mandatory reconciliation sign-off between approved amount, SFA value, and intended disbursement prior to fund release.
observations.managementResponse:
No remediation is required as tranche disbursements under an approved Supplementary Financing Agreement (SFA) are standard practice and remain within the approved exposure limit.

OWNER: HEAD CREDIT OPERATIONS

Audit Additional Comments
A discussion was had with the CSLA and the need to review the SFAs has been identified. Hence a remediation is required to mitigate further risks.

observations.title: Over-Reliance on AML Questionnaire Without Independent Validation or Ongoing Oversight
observations.description:
Over-Reliance on AML Questionnaire Without Independent Validation or Ongoing Oversight
The institution relies solely on completed AML/CFT questionnaires from PFIs to assess compliance, without independent verification or ongoing monitoring. There is no process to validate the accuracy of responses and no periodic monitoring or assurance over AML/CFT compliance at the end-beneficiary level.
observations.risk:
Increased regulatory risk and potential penalties for non-compliance with AML/CFT requirements.

Operational risk from inadequate monitoring and due diligence of end-beneficiaries.

Reputational risk if inadequate AML oversight is discovered by regulators or stakeholders.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Absence of independent verification procedures and periodic monitoring of AML/CFT responses.

System: Lack of automated monitoring tools to flag high-risk PFIs or beneficiaries for follow-up (e.g. world check).
observations.recommendation:
Implement ongoing monitoring and periodic review of AML/CFT compliance of PFIs and end-beneficiaries.

Leverage systems to track AML/CFT risks in PFIs and end-beneficiaries. 

Conduct independent validation of AML questionnaires received from PFIs, including sample checks and verification against supporting documentation.

Review existing exposures to identify any high-risk counterparties that may have been overlooked.
observations.managementResponse: Management will ensure that the AML/CFT check is formally carried out and documented during the anniversary due diligence of each Participating Financial Institution (PFI), to reinforce and support the AML/CFT review already conducted during onboarding due diligence.

observations.title: Inappropriate Classification of Master Financing Agreement as �Public� Document
observations.description:
Inappropriate Classification of Master Financing Agreement as �Public� Document
The Master Financing Agreement (MFA) with Abbey Mortgage Bank which governs the lending terms and commercial arrangements with the PFI, is classified as a �Public� document. Given the commercially sensitive nature of the terms contained therein (pricing, covenants, representations, default clauses), this classification exposes the institution to confidentiality and competitive risks.

Risk of unauthorized access to commercially sensitive credit terms.

Competitive disadvantage if pricing structures and credit terms become widely accessible.

Legal and reputational exposure in the event of information leakage.

observations.rootCause:

observations.recommendation:
Reclassify the Master Financing Agreement as �Confidential� or �Restricted� based on the approved information classification policy.

Develop and implement a formal document classification framework aligned with information security standards.
observations.managementResponse:
Management will reclassify the affected Master Financing Agreement as �Confidential� and configure document access controls to prevent the classification from being altered without appropriate authorization.

In addition, all existing Master Financing Agreements have been reviewed and confirmed to have the right classification status

observations.title: Absence of Independent Disbursement Confirmation Control
observations.description:
Absence of Independent Disbursement Confirmation Control 
Loan disbursements are initiated through instructions to BOI; however, the institution does not receive formal confirmation of execution date from the bank and does not obtain bank statements to independently verify value dates. Credit Operations therefore relies on informal confirmations (e.g., WhatsApp messages from PFIs) to determine when funds were received. This creates significant risk of incorrect loan effective dates, interest computation errors, and inaccurate portfolio reporting.
observations.risk:
Weak audit trail over cash disbursements and loan recognition.

Increased fraud and operational risk due to reliance on informal confirmations.

Regulatory risk where loan recognition is not supported by verifiable evidence.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: 
- No formal disbursement confirmation and reconciliation process with the bank.
- Inadequate control design over cash disbursement verification and loan activation.
observations.recommendation: Establish a formal requirement to obtain bank execution confirmation (transaction advice or statement extract) before loan activation.
observations.managementResponse: Disbursements are now being made directly from the Corporation�s CBN account. This enables independent confirmation of value dates and disbursement amounts through the Corporation�s own bank statements, eliminating reliance on third-party confirmations.

observations.title: PFI Exposure Concentration Above Approved Limit
observations.description:
PFI Exposure Concentration Above Approved Limit
We observed that exposure to certain PFIs exceeds the approved limit of 15% as set by the Management Risk Committee (MRC). Specifically, two PFIs have concentrations above the prescribed threshold as at 31 December 2025. 
Ecobank - 20%
Credit Direct - 16%

This breach of exposure limits increases the institution�s credit risk and reflects non-compliance with internal risk appetite and governance frameworks.
observations.risk:
Heightened credit risk due to over-concentration in a limited number of counterparties.

Potential financial loss if one of the overexposed PFIs defaults.

Non-compliance with risk management guidelines and internal approval limits.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause:
Process: Inadequate monitoring of PFI exposures relative to approved limits, especially considering the shrinking loan portfolio which increased concentration percentages.
People: Limited accountability for ensuring exposure thresholds are not breached.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately review exposures to the PFIs exceeding the limit and document management�s plan to reduce concentration (e.g., selective repayment, reallocation, or risk mitigation strategies).

Ensure periodic reporting to the MRC for oversight and approval of any exceptions, with clear accountability assigned for exposure management.

Implement a monitoring system or dashboard to track PFI exposures against approved limits, adjusting dynamically as the total portfolio changes.
observations.managementResponse:
The Corporation has now secured additional funding and resumed disbursements across other PFIs. As a result, exposure concentrations have normalized and are now within approved thresholds.

Going forward, exposure monitoring will continue to be aligned with the approved risk appetite limits to ensure compliance.

observations.title: Unauthorized Loan Restructuring Without Documentation or Approval
observations.description:
Unauthorized Loan Restructuring Without Documentation or Approval
A loan was restructured at the request of a PFI to extend the tenor; however, no restructuring memo or formal approval was documented. The policy requires the following:
- Risk Management assessment
- Legal assessment
- Submission of a restructuring proposal to MCIC

No evidence of these review requirements were seen in the ECOBANK file for the tenor restructuring of their loan.
observations.risk:
Increased credit risk due to unapproved extension of loan terms.

Potential misstatement of loan tenor, interest income, and repayment schedule.

Non-compliance with internal credit policies and regulatory expectations.

Weak audit trail, reducing transparency and accountability in loan management.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Absence of strict enforcement of documentation and approval requirements for loan restructurings.
People: Staff may implement restructuring requests without following formal approval channels.
observations.recommendation:
Document and obtain retroactive approval for the restructuring in line with credit policies.

Review other loan restructurings to ensure all were properly documented and authorized.

Revised SFA
observations.managementResponse:
Management has shared evidence of prior approval obtained from the Executive Director, Credit, Risk & Portfolio Management for the tenor extension.

An updated supplementary financing agreement has been shared with the affected PFI and would be signed and filed in the PFIs credit file.

observations.title: Absence of Standard Credit and Disbursement Memo Templates
observations.description:
Absence of Standard Credit and Disbursement Memo Templates 
There is no standard credit memo template in use, and no disbursement memos were observed � only onboarding due diligence reports were seen. Approval requests and disbursement documentation omit critical information, including collateral to be obtained and authorization for release of funds. This creates gaps in credit governance, increases the risk of incomplete or non-compliant approvals, and weakens the audit trail for loan disbursements.

Policy Requirement
A formal memorandum requesting onboarding and/or disbursement approval must be submitted to the MCIC by the Credit and Portfolio Management Department.
observations.risk:
Increased credit and operational risk due to incomplete documentation and approvals.

Potential misstatement of loan records, collateral coverage, and repayment terms.

Non-compliance with internal credit policies and regulatory expectations.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause: Process: No standardized templates for credit approval and loan disbursement documentation.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and implement standardized credit and disbursement memo templates capturing all key information (collateral, approvals, loan terms).

Enforce use of templates for all new credit approvals and disbursements.
observations.managementResponse: The credit and disbursement workflow has been embedded into the Loan Management System (LMS), which has been developed and will be fully deployed before Q1 2026 to enforce documentation completeness and approval controls.

observations.title: Inadequate Segregation of Duties in Credit Origination and Appraisal Process
observations.description:
Inadequate Segregation of Duties in Credit Origination and Appraisal Process
We observed that the same officer is responsible for loan sourcing, credit appraisal, and recommendation. This lack of segregation of duties creates a conflict of interest and increases the risk of biased assessments and override of credit standards. The absence of independent review weakens the integrity of the credit approval process.
observations.risk:
Increased risk of credit losses due to inadequate or biased credit assessment.

Higher susceptibility to fraud, collusion, or manipulation of credit analysis.

Weak governance and non-alignment with sound credit risk management principles.

Reduced reliability of credit recommendations submitted for approval.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: People: Limited staffing or resource constraints leading to role overlap.
observations.recommendation:
Introduce independent review (Risk & Compliance) of credit appraisals before submission for approval.

Reassign responsibilities to ensure separation between sourcing and appraisal functions where feasible. (Credit & Risk).

Explore additional staffing to drive effective SoD.
observations.managementResponse:
Management will continue to enforce the existing multi-layer review structure, whereby all onboarding due diligence reports are reviewed by Risk Management and subsequently approved by the Management Credit & Investment Committee (MCIC) prior to disbursement.

In addition, the approved organogram formally separates credit sourcing, appraisal, and review functions. Recruitment into these roles is underway to further strengthen operational segregation of duties and enhance independence within the credit process.

observations.title: Conflict Between PFI Offer Letter and SFA on End-Beneficiary Submission Timing
observations.description:
Conflict Between PFI Offer Letter and SFA on End-Beneficiary Submission Timing
The PFI offer letter requires submission of the end-beneficiary list prior to disbursement, whereas the Supplementary Financing Agreement (SFA) allows submission within 30 days post-disbursement. Operationally, pre-disbursement submission is impossible under the current lending model. This creates a misalignment between contractual documents and operational reality, weakening enforceability and clarity of monitoring obligations.
observations.risk:
Conflicting contractual requirements may cause disputes or confusion with PFIs.

Reduced effectiveness of beneficiary monitoring and control over fund utilization.

Legal, governance, and compliance risk due to misaligned documentation and policy.

RATING: LOW
observations.rootCause:
Policy/Legal: Offer letters drafted without considering practical disbursement workflow.
Process: No reconciliation between offer letters, SFAs, and operational procedures.
observations.recommendation:
Amend PFI offer letters to align with SFA provisions (i.e., allow post-disbursement submission within 30 days).

Implement standard templates for offer letters and SFAs reflecting operationally feasible timelines.
observations.managementResponse:
Offer letter templates  have been revised to align with the Supplementary Financing Agreement (SFA) provisions regarding post-disbursement submission timelines.

Standardized templates will be implemented to ensure consistency between contractual documents and operational workflow.

observations.title: Lack of Ongoing Review Process for KYC Documentation
observations.description:
Lack of Ongoing Review Process for KYC Documentation
We observed that there is no formal process for periodic review of KYC documents (e.g., ID cards) to ensure they remain valid. During the audit, some KYC documents were expired, although these were remediated before audit closure. The absence of a continuous review process increases the risk of relying on outdated or invalid customer information.
observations.risk:
Increased compliance risk with AML/CFT regulations.

Reduced assurance over the integrity of the customer onboarding and monitoring process.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause:
Process: No structured periodic KYC review or renewal workflow.
People: Responsibility for monitoring document validity is not clearly assigned.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately identify all expired KYC documents and ensure updates are obtained.

Implement a formal KYC review schedule.

Assign clear ownership for KYC validity monitoring.

Integrate KYC validity checks into ongoing monitoring and periodic compliance reporting.
observations.managementResponse:
All expired KYC documents have now been updated.

The existing KYC tracking process, previously maintained via Excel and reviewed quarterly, has now been automated within the Loan Management System (LMS). The system will automatically prompt PFIs when KYC documents are due to expire to ensure timely renewal.

observations.title: Inconsistencies and Ambiguities in Loan Tenor and Repayment Term Documentation
observations.description:
Inconsistencies and Ambiguities in Loan Tenor and Repayment Term Documentation
We observed weaknesses in the clarity, consistency, and alignment of approved loan tenor and repayment terms across credit approval, customer communication, and legal documentation.

Specifically:
1. Misalignment Between Approved and Communicated Loan Tenor: A loan facility (Fast Credit 117) approved for a 24-month tenor was communicated and structured as 23 months.

2. Ambiguity in Tenor and Repayment Provisions in SFAs:  Supplementary Financing Agreements (SFAs) use broad language such as �for periods not exceeding 2 years� or �not exceeding 4 years� without specifying the exact tenor.
observations.risk:
Contractual ambiguity affecting enforceability

Inconsistent loan monitoring and repayment tracking

Potential disputes over loan structure and obligations

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Absence of a review control to validate consistency between approved credit terms and communicated/executed loan documentation prior to disbursement.

System: No system-enforced validation to restrict change of approved tenor in repayment schedule without formal re-approval.
observations.recommendation:
Where contractually permissible, formally regularize the tenor to align with the approved credit terms or obtain proper ratification for the deviation.

Standardize SFA templates with explicitly defined tenor and repayment frequency.
observations.managementResponse: The Supplementary Financing Agreement (SFA) template has been updated to explicitly state loan tenor and repayment frequency.

observations.title: Treasury Bills Pledged as Collateral Are Not Legally Perfected or Enforceable
observations.description:
Treasury Bills Pledged as Collateral Are Not Legally Perfected or Enforceable
We observed that treasury bills pledged by PFIs as collateral are not registered in the institution�s favor, there is no custodian arrangement, and no legal review has been conducted. The institution only holds letters from PFIs pledging the securities. As a result, the collateral may not be enforceable in the event of PFI default.
observations.risk:
High credit risk exposure due to inability to recover or liquidate pledged collateral.

Potential financial loss in case of PFI default.

Weak legal and operational controls over high-value collateral.

Regulatory and governance risk due to inadequate collateral security documentation.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: No formal procedure to perfect or verify collateral for enforceability.
People: Responsibility for collateral perfection and legal validation is not clearly assigned.
Governance: Lack of oversight to ensure pledged securities are legally enforceable before disbursement.
observations.recommendation:
Engage legal counsel immediately to assess existing pledged T-bills and identify enforceability gaps.

Formalize a custodial or registration arrangement for all T-bills pledged going forward.

Integrate legal review of all collateral documentation into the credit approval process.
observations.managementResponse:
The Finance Department has secured a Treasury Bills custodian and is currently finalizing the required documentation and custodial arrangements.

Upon completion, the Corporation will coordinate with the relevant PFIs to transfer and formally lodge pledged Treasury Bills under the custodial structure to ensure legal perfection and enforceability.

observations.title: Inability to Trace Loan Repayment Collections to Bank Statements
observations.description:
Inability to Trace Loan Repayment Collections to Bank Statements
We were unable to trace loan repayment collections totaling over ?160 million to the CBN bank statements. There was no clear reconciliation or trail linking recorded repayments to actual cash inflows.

This raises concerns over completeness, accuracy, and transparency of repayment recording.
observations.risk:
Risk of misstatement of loan balances and income recognition.

Weak cash management and reconciliation controls.

Reduced reliability of financial reporting.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Absence of periodic independent loan-to-bank reconciliation process.

Lack of structured documentation linking repayment schedules, ledger postings, and bank credits.
observations.recommendation:
Perform a full reconciliation of all repayments recorded versus bank inflows.

Implement monthly independent reconciliation for collections.
observations.managementResponse:
All Remita receipts evidencing repayments have been shared with the Finance Department. Finance has confirmed the inflows and ensured that the amounts were appropriately posted into the EazyBank system.

Audit may liaise directly with Finance to independently validate reconciliation between Remita receipts, bank inflows, and ledger postings.

OWNER: CHIEF FINANCE OFFICER (CFO)

Audit Comment
Reconciliations are ongoing with the finance team.

observations.title: Lack of Reconciled Liability Schedules
observations.description:
Lack of Reconciled Liability Schedules
We observed that liability accounts do not have reconciled schedules showing outstanding or yet-to-be-paid items. Monthly reconciliation of asset and liability accounts is not being performed, resulting in incomplete visibility of balances. This increases the risk of errors or omissions in financial reporting and operational decision-making.
observations.risk:
Increased risk of misstatement in financial reports.

Potential for missed or duplicate payments, leading to operational inefficiency and financial loss.

Reduced ability to manage liquidity effectively.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Absence of a formalized monthly reconciliation procedure for liability accounts.
observations.recommendation:
Finance to prepare and reconcile liability schedules immediately to identify outstanding balances and validate completeness.

Implement a monthly reconciliation process with assigned ownership and sign-off within the finance team.
observations.managementResponse: Finance is finalizing the schedules and will share them as soon as they are ready

observations.title: Overstatement of Payroll Expense in the Trial Balance
observations.description:
Overstatement of Payroll Expense in the Trial Balance
Payroll expenses in the trial balance were found to be overstated compared to supporting payroll records. The discrepancy was due to unverified entries and lack of timely adjustments for corrections. This results in inaccurate reporting of personnel costs and financial position.
observations.risk:
Misstated financial statements and potential non-compliance with accounting standards.

Risk of overpayment or misallocation of funds.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Inadequate review and reconciliation between payroll records and the general ledger prior to posting.
observations.recommendation:
Reconcile payroll records with the trial balance immediately to identify and correct overstated amounts.

Implement a monthly payroll reconciliation process with documented sign-off by the supervisor.
observations.managementResponse:
The variance identified was primarily due to the 13th month payment and the bonus tied to Credicoins. This reconciliation was jointly carried out by Internal Audit and the Finance Department. However, the People and Culture Department is required to confirm the accuracy of the payroll schedule that was provided to the Internal Audit team

OWNER: CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

Audit additional Comment
The credicoins should be reclassified as expense or be treated appropriately based on its nature.
Another reconciliation is to be performed for Q1 2026 prior to closure of this observation.

observations.title: System Over-Accrual of Interest Income Due to Extra Day in Year-End Computation
observations.description:
System Over-Accrual of Interest Income Due to Extra Day in Year-End Computation
The loan management system added an extra day when computing accrued interest for loans not yet billed as at 31 December 2025. This resulted in an over-accrual of interest income of >?10 million for affected loans. Consequently, accrued interest income and loan asset balances were materially misstated at year-end.
observations.risk:
Overstatement of interest income and loan assets in the financial statements.

Misstatement of year-end performance.

Risk of recurring errors if the system logic is not corrected.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause:
System: Loan management system incorrectly picks an extra day when calculating accrued interest for year-end for some loans.

Process: No validation of system-generated accruals prior to financial close.
observations.recommendation:
Recompute interest accruals for all affected loans to remove the extra day and adjust the trial balance accordingly.

Correct the system logic to prevent addition of the extra day in future year-end accruals.

Implement a pre-close review process to validate system-generated interest accruals.
observations.managementResponse: The interest income is automatically computed by the EasyBank solution. Any discrepancies identified by the Internal Audit Department have been escalated to the vendor for review, while finance is currently reviewing all the interest computed on the loan for accuracy.

observations.title: Absence of Documented Close Timetable and Escalation Protocol
observations.description:
Absence of Documented Close Timetable and Escalation Protocol
We noted that there is no documented or consistently practiced month-end, quarter-end, or year-end financial close timetable. Responsibilities, deadlines, and escalation protocols for delays are not clearly assigned. This creates uncertainty in the close process and increases the risk of errors and delays in financial reporting.
observations.risk:
Delayed delivery of management accounts, ALCO reports, and other critical financial statements.

Increased likelihood of rushed adjustments, misstatements, and omission of key information.

Weak control environment over the financial close process, reducing reliability of reported results.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause: Process: Lack of a formal, documented close schedule and defined responsibilities.
observations.recommendation:
Implement a documented month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close timetable with clearly assigned responsibilities.

Establish a formal escalation protocol for any delays or issues during the close process.

Monitor adherence to the timetable through management review and periodic reviews.
observations.managementResponse:
Our SOP clearly outlines the month end closure of all entries into the easy bank.

OWNER: CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

Audit additional Comment
This is noted. Review of SOP documentation will be carried out prior to closure. 

However, part of the issues is adherence to timelines for period close activities. Kindly ensure implementation of the timetable.

observations.title: Decentralized Storage of Financial Documentation and Insufficient Transaction Support
observations.description:
Decentralized Storage of Financial Documentation and Insufficient Transaction Support
During the review of journal entries and selected financial transactions, it was observed that supporting documentation is stored in a decentralized manner, including individual email inboxes. No centralized repository exists to ensure consistent retention and accessibility of financial records. In some cases, the documentation provided was insufficient to substantiate the validity of the transactions.
observations.risk:
Increased risk of financial misstatements and unsupported transactions.

Hinders auditability and timely verification of financial records.

Operational inefficiency due to difficulty in retrieving documentation for review or investigation.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Absence of a centralized document management process for financial records.
observations.recommendation:
Collect and consolidate all existing supporting documents into a temporary centralized repository pending implementation of a DMS. 

Implement a centralized, secure document management system for all financial records (DMS).
observations.managementResponse: Finance will ensure that a centralised data storage system is instituted.

observations.title: Unusual Year-End Accrued Salaries Balance
observations.description:
Unusual Year-End Accrued Salaries Balance
As at 31 December 2025, an accrued salaries balance of ?1.013 million was recorded, despite there being no outstanding staff liabilities. This indicates an overstatement of liabilities in the financial statements. The balance should have been nil as at year-end, reflecting no unpaid salaries.
observations.risk:
Overstatement of liabilities, leading to misrepresentation of the company�s financial position.

Weakness in payroll accrual and financial close controls, increasing risk of similar misstatements.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause:
Process: Lack of review and clearance of salary accruals at year-end. 
Lack of process for verification of salary/payroll monthly details prior to payment/posting.
observations.recommendation:
Reconcile all payroll-related accruals to ensure accuracy in the trial balance.

Implement a year-end payroll accrual review checklist to verify all balances before closing.

Assign accountability for reconciliation and approval of payroll accruals.
observations.managementResponse: The employee pension payment was initially processed but subsequently reversed by the payment system. The payment has now been reprocessed and successfully completed in 2026. The outstanding balance does not relate to salary accruals but to the previously reversed pension payment, which has since been fully settled.

observations.title: Inefficient and Uncontrolled General Ledger Structure (Chart of Accounts)
observations.description:
Inefficient and Uncontrolled General Ledger Structure (Chart of Accounts)
During review of the General Ledger and Chart of Accounts (CoA), it was observed that many accounts are inactive or unused. There is no documented process for periodic review, rationalization, or formal approval for creation, modification, or deactivation of accounts. Additionally, some accounts have similar descriptions (e.g., Medical Expenses & Staff Medical Insurance), increasing the risk of inconsistent postings.
observations.risk:
Higher likelihood of misposting transactions due to ambiguous or duplicate accounts.

Increased complexity and inefficiency in financial reporting and reconciliation processes.

Weak control environment for GL maintenance, potentially leading to misstated financial statements.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Absence of a formalized GL review and rationalization procedure. No approval framework for changes to the CoA.
observations.recommendation:
Conduct a one-time rationalization of the GL, deactivating unused accounts and merging duplicate or overlapping accounts. (This should be done in collaboration with Internal Control).

Implement a documented CoA maintenance and rationalization policy.

Establish an approval framework for creation, modification, or deactivation of GL accounts. (Can be part of an existing policy or SOP).
observations.managementResponse:
Since the banking solution is still in the early stages of deployment, we understand that the Chart of Accounts (COA) will need to be reviewed and adjusted at a later time. 

Action date: 31 March 2026

observations.title: Absence of Documented Related Party Identification and Monitoring
observations.description:
Absence of Documented Related Party Identification and Monitoring
The institution does not have a documented process for identifying related parties. There is no formal mechanism, such as annual declarations or a register, to capture related party relationships, and no structured review is performed during the financial close process to identify related party transactions. Consequently, completeness and accuracy of related party disclosures in financial reporting cannot be assured.
observations.risk:
Risk of incomplete or inaccurate related party disclosures, potentially violating accounting standards and regulatory requirements.

Increased risk of conflicts of interest or undisclosed related party dealings.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Lack of formal procedures for identification, declaration, and review of related parties. 
Governance: No oversight or accountability assigned for monitoring related party relationships and transactions.
observations.recommendation:
Implement a formal related party identification process, including annual declarations and a maintained register.

Integrate related party review into the financial close checklist to ensure completeness.

Assign accountability to a responsible officer or committee to oversee ongoing monitoring.
observations.managementResponse:
We do not have any related party transaction. 

OWNER: CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

Audit additional Comment
There must be a documented and demonstrable process supporting this conclusion. This should include evidence of nil related party declarations, in addition to the Corporation�s related party policy.

observations.title: Delayed Remittance of Withholding Tax, VAT & Pension Remittances
observations.description:
Delayed Remittance of Withholding Tax, VAT & Pension Remittances
1. We noted evidence of unremitted WHT and VAT obligations to the relevant authorities. Some deductions, including WHT for E. Consulting (?39.9m) and Paul A. (?7.75m) from December 2024, remain outstanding in the Accrued WHT and Accrued VAT ledgers. Remittances are required by the 21st day of the month following deduction, and delays constitute non-compliance with statutory obligations.

2. As at 31 December 2025, the unremitted pension obligation was ?65.16 million, while the expected outstanding based on the payroll schedule (December salaries and Q4 allowances) was ?22.26 million. This indicates an overdue/unremitted liability of ?42.9 million. Pension contributions are required by law to be remitted within seven working days of salary payment, and the delay constitutes non-compliance.
observations.risk:
Risk of penalties, fines, and interest charges from tax authorities.

Operational risk due to lack of timely tracking and payment of statutory obligations.

Reputational risk and reduced employee confidence in statutory compliance.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Lack of a structured process for timely tracking and remittance of statutory deductions.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately remit all outstanding WHT, VAT, and Pension obligations to relevant authorities.

Implement a structured schedule for monitoring and remitting WHT, VAT, and Pension obligations.

Assign clear accountability for tax remittances and incorporate compliance checks into the financial close process.
observations.managementResponse:
The Finance department was previously operating with only one dedicated staff member, supported intermittently by a resource from another department. This limited capacity resulted in delays in making some tax payments when they became due. Despite these constraints, all outstanding taxes have now been fully settled up to 31 December 2025. Going forward, tax obligations have been scheduled to be paid on a monthly basis as they fall due, ensuring full compliance and improved operational efficiency.

observations.title: Net Basis Posting of Capital Asset Transactions Increasing Risk of Misstatement
observations.description:
Net Basis Posting of Capital Asset Transactions Increasing Risk of Misstatement
Some capital asset transactions are posted on a net basis, reflecting only the payment made to the vendor. While statutory deductions such as VAT, WHT, and stamp duty are typically booked subsequently, the reliance on manual follow-up creates a risk that deductions may be missed. This practice increases the likelihood of misstatement in the accounts and non-compliance with statutory obligations.
observations.risk:
Risk of missing statutory deductions if subsequent entries are forgotten, leading to penalties, interest, or regulatory scrutiny.

Reduced auditability and transparency of capital asset acquisitions.

Operational risk due to reliance on manual follow-up and potential human error.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Lack of a policy enforcing gross posting of capital asset transactions and immediate recording of statutory deductions.

People: Staff may rely on subsequent manual postings, increasing the chance of oversight.
observations.recommendation:
Reconcile past net postings to verify that all statutory obligations have been captured.

Implement a formal finance manual requiring and guiding on the gross posting of capital asset acquisitions with statutory deductions recorded at the time of entry.
observations.managementResponse: All asset-related components were recorded in the month in which they were incurred, and the tax components were accurately captured and paid without difficulty. However, if Internal Audit requires a specific format to facilitate their review, the Finance Department is willing to adopt it, provided that such a format does not conflict with applicable accounting standards.

observations.title: Delayed Implementation and Lack of Review of Bank Reconciliations
observations.description:
Delayed Implementation and Lack of Review of Bank Reconciliations
The corporation only commenced formal bank reconciliations in November 2025. There is no evidence that reconciliation statements were reviewed or that reconciling items were communicated to relevant stakeholders for monitoring. This weakens internal control over cash, increases the risk of undetected errors or fraud, and limits oversight of outstanding items.

Update
We were unable to trace some recorded repayments to the Corporations bank statements for Q4 2025, however, these transactions do not reflect as outstanding items on the bank reconciliation statement, hence this elevates the risk and impact of this finding.
observations.risk:
Increased risk of misstatement in cash and bank balances reported in the financial statements.

Unmonitored reconciling items could lead to delayed detection of errors or fraudulent transactions.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Process: Absence of a formal review and communication process for bank reconciliations.
observations.recommendation:
Implement a formal bank reconciliation process with documented review and approval workflow.

Assign accountability for reconciliation review and monitoring of reconciling items.
observations.managementResponse: The finance department has a version of the reviewed bank reconciliation. Kindly meet with Tubolayefa George to give you an updated reconciliation report.

observations.title: Lack of Regular Analytical Reviews
observations.description:
Lack of Regular Analytical Reviews
Analytical reviews are not performed at set frequencies, such as monthly. Consequently, there was no variance analysis against budget or prior periods, and no evidence of investigation into unusual movements. This lack of regular analytical review increases the risk that material misstatements in financial statements remain undetected and uncorrected.
observations.risk:
Increased likelihood of undetected financial errors or irregular transactions.

Weakens management oversight and reduces the reliability of financial reporting.

Potential delay in corrective actions for anomalies, affecting decision-making.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause: Process: Absence of a formal schedule or requirement for periodic analytical reviews. Lack of oversight and formal procedures to ensure timely variance and trend analysis.
observations.recommendation:
Implement a formal schedule for analytical reviews (e.g., monthly) comparing actuals vs budget and prior periods.

Assign accountability for conducting and reviewing variance analysis.
observations.managementResponse: The Finance Department routinely performs analytical reviews of expenditures, and necessary adjustments are made whenever unusual transactions are identified.

observations.title: Lack of Management Review of Financial Statements
observations.description:
Lack of Management Review of Financial Statements
There is no evidence that financial statements or management accounts are reviewed by management. The absence of review reflects weak governance oversight and contravenes relevant accounting, regulatory, and internal control standards. This exposes the institution to risks of errors, misstatements, and undetected irregularities in reporting.
observations.risk:
Increased risk of material misstatements remaining undetected in financial statements.

Reduces reliability and credibility of financial reporting to stakeholders.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause:
Process: Lack of formalized procedure requiring management review and sign-off of financial statements.
People: Limited assignment of accountability for reviewing and approving financial reports.
observations.recommendation:
Implement a formal review and approval process for all financial statements and management accounts.

Assign clear responsibility and accountability for review, with sign-off documented.
observations.managementResponse: Management Team remained consistently updated on the management accounts through regular email communication. Their feedback and reviews were also obtained during meetings such as ALCO and MANCO.

observations.title: Absence of Formal Asset Identification and Tagging Exercise
observations.description:
Absence of Formal Asset Identification and Tagging Exercise
During the audit, it was observed that the corporation has not conducted a formal asset identification and tagging exercise across the organization. Consequently, management has not been able to reconfirm the completeness and accuracy of the asset register against assets physically in use across the Coporation.
observations.risk:
Increases the risk of incomplete or inaccurate asset records, potential loss or misappropriation of assets, and difficulty in safeguarding and tracking assets across locations.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Lack of a structured asset management framework and absence of periodic asset verification exercises.
observations.recommendation: Management should conduct a comprehensive asset identification and tagging exercise across all locations and reconcile the results with the asset register. An annual asset verification process should be institutionalized.
observations.managementResponse: A new vendor has been identified, and we are presently awaiting the submission of his invoice as well as the comparative invoices from other vendors we reached out to.

observations.title: Absence of Standardized Asset Tagging Framework
observations.description:
Absence of Standardized Asset Tagging Framework
Although asset tags/numbers exist on the fixed asset register on Eazybank, there is no documented standard defining the structure of the asset tag number or the meaning of each field within the tag. 

Some codes could not be interpreted, while others had tags containing "ZZZ� placeholders without documented explanation.
observations.risk:
Lack of a standardized tagging framework may lead to inconsistencies in asset identification, difficulty in tracking assets, and potential errors in asset recording and monitoring.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause: Absence of documented procedures governing asset tagging standards and exception management.
observations.recommendation:
Develop and document a standardized asset tagging framework that defines the structure, coding logic, and interpretation of each component of the asset tag.

Update
The dictionary was obtained, however, the location tags needs to be sanitized to reflect operational realities
observations.managementResponse:
The CFO explained that EasyBank is currently working on it, and they have not yet finalized what the appropriate code for the unassigned asset should be. However, the CFO is in the best position to provide further clarification on what this means.

Audit Update:
Accountability for asset management rests with Admin.

observations.title: Unexplained Gaps in Fixed Asset Register Serial Number Sequence
observations.description:
Unexplained Gaps in Fixed Asset Register Serial Number Sequence
Certain serial numbers within the Fixed Asset Register sequence were missing. While some were linked to asset disposals or rebooked entries, several sequence gaps could not be explained, and no reconciliation exists to account for the missing entries.
observations.risk:
Weak register integrity may increase the risk of unauthorized asset additions, deletions, or manipulation of asset records.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause: Lack of formal controls over asset register maintenance and absence of periodic reconciliation.
observations.recommendation: Management should perform a reconciliation of the asset register and document explanations for all sequence gaps. Controls should be implemented to ensure proper audit trails for asset additions and disposals.
observations.managementResponse: The Internal Audit and Finance units will review this and will take an appropriate position thereafter

observations.title: Absence of Insurance Coverage for Organizational Assets
observations.description:
Absence of Insurance Coverage for Organizational Assets
The organization does not maintain insurance coverage for its physical assets, including buildings, equipment, and vehicles.
observations.risk:
Exposes the organization to potentially significant financial losses in the event of theft, fire, natural disaster, or other unforeseen incidents affecting assets.

RATING: HIGH
observations.rootCause: Absence of a formal asset risk management and insurance strategy.
observations.recommendation: Management should conduct a risk assessment of critical assets and obtain appropriate insurance coverage.
observations.managementResponse:
Efforts are on the way to pay for the all-assets insurance.

In addition, comprehensive insurance is to be provided for motor vehicles by the suppliers. This is also in progress

observations.title: Absence of Signed Delivery Notes to Evidence Receipt of Assets
observations.description:
Absence of Signed Delivery Notes to Evidence Receipt of Assets
During the review of procurement and payment documentation, it was observed that certain delivery notes related to purchased items were not signed or acknowledged by the corporation to confirm receipt of the goods delivered. As a result, there is no documented evidence confirming that the items invoiced were physically received by the organization and the exact date of receipt.
observations.risk:
The absence of signed delivery notes increases the risk of payments being made for goods not delivered or delivered in incomplete quantities. 

In addition, it limits management�s ability to accurately determine the date assets were placed in service, which may result in incorrect depreciation start dates and potential inaccuracies in financial reporting.

RATING: MEDIUM
observations.rootCause: Weak controls over goods receipt confirmation and lack of enforcement of documentation requirements prior to invoice approval and payment processing.
observations.recommendation: Management should ensure that all goods received are supported by properly signed and dated delivery notes or Goods Received Notes (GRNs) confirming the receipt, quantity, and condition of items delivered before vendor invoices are processed for payment.
observations.managementResponse:
We had to make a correction on one of the cars� delivery notes when it was delivered, so you probably reviewed the version that required the correction. However, if there are any delivery notes that were not signed, please share them with us so we can have them signed immediately.

Audit update: The unsigned notes sighted have been shared, however, these were based on very limited samples reviewed. It is imperative that the practice is implemented and enforced as this is critical is confirming asset availability for use.

observations.title: Assets Received but Not Supported by Vendor Invoice
observations.description:
Assets Received but Not Supported by Vendor Invoice
During the review of asset additions, it was observed that the corporation paid for 10 computer monitors; however, 11 computer monitors were physically received and recorded in the asset register. The total cost was allocated across 11 units despite only 10 units being invoiced by the vendor. This indicates that an asset was received without a corresponding invoice or recorded liability.
observations.risk: This exposes the organization to the risk of understated liabilities and inaccurate financial reporting.
observations.recommendation: A reconciliation of assets received but not invoiced should be performed, and any outstanding vendor liabilities should be identified and recorded.
observations.managementResponse: The overall invoice amount of ?165,075,211.01 is correct. However, the supply of 11 monitors was included in the payment to avoid leaving an outstanding balance with the vendor, which could have created additional liabilities

observations.title: Engagement of Vendors Without Formal Contracts
observations.description:
Engagement of Vendors Without Formal Contracts
The review identified instances where vendors were engaged and services commenced based solely on award letters, without the execution of formal contracts. (e.g. EBIS supply of IT equipments, 2 contracts for EBIS not drafted and executed, TiwaLinks)

Asides the award letters, comprehensive contractual agreements are required to contain critical elements such as:

- Defined scope of services
- Service level expectations
- Roles and responsibilities
- Liability and indemnity provisions
- Termination and dispute resolution clauses
- Data protection and confidentiality requirements
observations.risk:
- Limited legal enforceability of vendor obligations
- Inability to effectively manage or enforce service performance
- Potential disputes arising from unclear expectations and responsibilities
observations.rootCause: Weak enforcement of contract execution controls prior to vendor onboarding
observations.recommendation:
- Enforce a strict �No Contract, No Service� policy, ensuring that all vendor engagements are governed by duly executed contracts prior to service commencement.
- Conduct a retrospective regularization exercise to formalize contracts for all existing vendors currently operating without executed agreements.
- Contract register should be updated and documents filled appropriately by the legal department.
observations.managementResponse:
This observation had previously been identified by the Risk and Compliance Department, and the Procurement Department has collaborated with the Legal Department to ensure the execution of Service Level Agreements (SLAs) before contract commences subject to the avilabilty of Management to perfect the instruments.

In addition, a strengthened control measure has been institutionalized, whereby no contract award letter is issued without a duly executed SLA (�No SLA, No Award Letter� policy). This is to ensure that contractual obligations, service expectations, and performance metrics are clearly defined prior to contract commencement.

Award letter shall hencforth be released by Legal Department to ensure all contractual requirements are fulfillied.

observations.title: Observations in Vendor Performance Evaluation and Remediation Framework
observations.description:
The review of vendor performance management processes identified gaps in the coverage, evaluation, and remediation of vendor performance.

Specifically:

1. Vendor performance assessments are conducted solely by designated contract owners without incorporating structured input from other users of the service, particularly for vendors providing organization-wide services (e.g., HMO, IT support). Whilst having a single responder drives accountability, it ensure a balanced view, for certain services/vendors feedback from different stakeholders should be obtained.

2. Certain high-value vendors were not included in the formal performance evaluation process, with no documented rationale for their exclusion or evidence of alternative structured assessments. (e.g. TiwaLinks, Intermac, Grey Fusion)

3. While vendor performance issues and corrective actions are documented, the remediation process lacks clearly defined action owners, timelines, and formal tracking to closure.
observations.risk:
- Incomplete or biased assessment of vendor performance
- Limited oversight of high-value and high-impact vendor relationships
- Failure to identify service delivery issues experienced by end users
- Reduced assurance of value for money for significant vendor spend
observations.rootCause:
- Absence of a risk-based vendor performance management framework
- Lack of a formalized multi-stakeholder evaluation process
observations.recommendation:
- Adopt a risk-based approach to vendor evaluation, ensuring that all high-value and critical vendors are included in periodic performance assessments. There should also be clear assignment of action owners, defined timelines and priority levels for vendor issues identified.
