- Enhancing performance evaluations to incorporate structured feedback from relevant stakeholders, particularly for vendors providing services across multiple user groups, while retaining accountability with the contract owner.
observations.managementResponse: The Audit team may note that all vendors were prequalified, hence the risk of non-perfomance have been properly addressed. However, the Gap noted by the Audit team with respect to perfomance appraisal would be addressed with a weighted performance rating systems going forward as the organization continue to engage new hands to fill vacant roles.

observations.title: Observations in Technical Evaluation and Documentation for Consultant Selection
observations.description:
The following was observed in the review of consultant selection processes:

- Technical evaluations are conducted collectively by the evaluation committee, without evidence of independent scoring by individual members. This reduces objectivity and increases the risk of bias or dominance by certain committee members.

- In addition, for procurements reviewed, while the selected bidder had the highest technical score, there was no supporting documentation, such as rating sheets or individual scoring records, demonstrating how these scores were derived. Consequently, the evaluation outcome cannot be independently verified.
observations.risk:
- Limited ability to verify and substantiate evaluation outcomes
- Weak audit trail for procurement decisions, which may be challenged internally or externally
- Inadequate transparency and accountability in awarding high-value contracts
observations.rootCause: - Lack of policy enforcement requiring independent scoring and documentation
observations.recommendation:
Management should strengthen the technical evaluation process by:
- Requiring independent scoring by each evaluation committee member, particularly for high-value or technical procurements.
- Documenting all technical evaluations with individual rating sheets and justification notes, consolidated into a summary report for audit purposes.
- Clearly defining evaluation methodology, criteria, and weighting in procurement policies and enforcing compliance.
observations.managementResponse: The Department is set to extend further training to nominees from other user department on the issue raised by the Audit Team Going forward.

observations.title: Absence of Independent Cost Estimates to Validate Bid Pricing
observations.description:
The review of procurement processes identified that independent in-house cost estimates were not consistently prepared to assess the reasonableness of vendor pricing.

This was particularly noted in instances where single bids were received, and there was no documented benchmark to validate whether the quoted prices were competitive or aligned with market rates.
observations.risk:
- Increased risk of overpricing and inflated procurement costs
- Weak assurance of value for money in procurement decisions
observations.rootCause:
Absence of a formal requirement for independent cost estimation
Weak procurement planning and cost benchmarking processes
observations.recommendation:
- Establish a requirement for independent in-house cost estimates for procurements, particularly for high-value transactions and single-bid or limited competition scenarios

- Develop standardized methodologies for preparing estimates, including: Market price benchmarking, Historical data analysis, Industry rate references

- Ensure cost estimates are documented and approved prior to bid evaluation.
observations.managementResponse: The audit team may wish to note that market survey base prices exists on all the procurement conducted. However, the in-house estimates would be considered a mandatory document in all procurement going forward.

observations.title: Absence of Sanctions and Watchlist Screening in Vendor Due Diligence
observations.description:
Absence of Sanctions and Watchlist Screening in Vendor Due Diligence
While vendor due diligence procedures cover legal, financial, and capability assessments, there is no evidence of sanctions or watchlist screening performed during vendor onboarding.
observations.risk: This may expose the organization to potential reputational or compliance risks, particularly in cases where vendors may be linked to restricted or high-risk entities.
observations.rootCause: N/A - Advisory observation
observations.recommendation: Management may consider incorporating sanctions and watchlist screening as part of the vendor onboarding process, particularly for high-risk or critical vendors.
observations.managementResponse: The Procurement Department shall seek the collaborations of Legal, Compliance and Risks Management Departments on the Sanctions, PEP, and watchlist screening as additional due diligence on procurement activities going forward.

observations.title: Absence of a Central Vendor Risk Rating Framework
observations.description:
Absence of a Central Vendor Risk Rating Framework
The review of third-party management practices identified the absence of a formal, centralized vendor risk rating or segmentation framework to classify vendors based on their inherent risk exposure.

There is no documented methodology to categorize vendors based on key risk indicators such as:

- Criticality of services provided
- Access to sensitive or confidential data
- Financial exposure or contract value
- Operational dependency
- Cybersecurity or IT system access

As a result, vendors appear to be managed in a largely uniform manner, without differentiation based on risk level or business impact.
observations.risk:
- Inability to prioritize high-risk or critical vendors for enhanced monitoring
- Increased exposure to unidentified or unmanaged third-party risks
- Weak alignment with third-party risk management best practices
observations.rootCause:
- Lack of a formalized third-party risk management framework
- Absence of standardized vendor segmentation criteria within procurement or risk governance processes
observations.recommendation:
Management should establish a centralized vendor risk rating framework that:

- Classifies vendors into risk tiers (e.g., Critical, High, Medium, Low) based on defined criteria such as: Data sensitivity, Operational dependency, Financial exposure, Regulatory impact.

- Links risk classification to: Due diligence requirements, Frequency of performance reviews, Audit coverage and depth.

- Ensures periodic review and updating of vendor risk ratings based on changing business conditions.
observations.managementResponse: As the Procurement Department continues its engagement with IT Department on the proposed development and deployment of procurement portal, the risk categories of vendor shall be included as added features for the use of Compliance Unit.

observations.title: Weaknesses in Data Protection Governance and Compliance Framework
observations.description:
Weaknesses in Data Protection Governance and Compliance Framework
The Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) requires organisations processing personal data to establish adequate governance, compliance, and awareness measures to ensure the protection of personal data. Internal Audit observed the following gaps in the corporation�s data protection framework: 
1. No Data Protection Officer (DPO) has been appointed, and no formal appointment letter defining roles, responsibilities, reporting lines, and authority was provided for review. 
2. No evidence of a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) conducted on personal data processing activities was provided. 
3. The corporation has not registered with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), despite the scale and nature of operations indicating that the requirement is applicable. 
4. No evidence of data protection awareness or training for staff was provided for review.
observations.risk:
Failure to appoint a DPO exposes the corporation to:

- Regulatory sanctions and penalties
- Weak oversight of data privacy compliance
- Increased risk of data breaches and non-compliance
observations.rootCause: The corporation�s Data Protection Policy was only recently developed, and implementation of the requirements of the NDPA is still ongoing. In addition, delays in the procurement and engagement processes required to support implementation activities have contributed to the slow rollout of key data protection governance and compliance measures.
observations.recommendation:
Management should strengthen the corporation�s data protection governance framework by:
- Appointing a qualified Data Protection Officer (DPO) and issuing a formal appointment letter defining responsibilities and reporting lines. 
- Conducting a comprehensive Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) covering all relevant data processing activities and documenting mitigation measures. 
- Completing registration with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC). 
- Implementing mandatory periodic data protection awareness and training programs for all staff.
observations.managementResponse: 1. Finalize appointment of the Corporation�s Data Protection Officer (DPO) and issue formal appointment letter through HR. 2. Complete procurement and engagement of a qualified data protection/compliance vendor to support a comprehensive DPIA and broader NDPA compliance implementation. 3. Commence registration process with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC). 4. Implement periodic staff data protection awareness and NDPA compliance training programs.

observations.title: Lack of Organisational Independence of the Risk Management Function
observations.description:
Lack of Organisational Independence of the Risk Management Function
Corporate governance and regulatory best practices require the Risk Management function to be independent of business/revenue-generating functions to ensure objective risk oversight and effective challenge of management decisions.

The Risk function is expected to maintain functional independence and avoid reporting lines that may impair objectivity or create conflicts of interest.

Internal Audit observed that the Head of Risk reports to the Executive Director, Credit Portfolio. The following business units also report to the same Executive Director: Credit Operations, Ecosystem Development, Cultural Reorientation, Fund Raising.

This reporting structure functionally impedes the independence of the risk management function.

In addition, the risk management function is required by the CBN Code of Corporate Governance to report directly to the Board Committees in charge of risk. However, we observed that the organogram is not in accordance with this requirement.
observations.risk:
This structure may impair the independence and effectiveness of the Risk function and exposes the organisation to:

- Conflict of interest in risk oversight and credit decision processes
- Reduced ability of Risk to challenge business and credit decisions objectively
- Weak implementation of the Three Lines of Defence model
- Increased exposure to regulatory criticism and governance findings
observations.rootCause:
It was as a result of the organization's start-up and lean operating structure, under which certain functions were grouped for administrative oversight and operational efficiency during the Corporation�s early-stage setup.

At the time, the structure was designed to support agility, resource optimization, and close coordination across related business functions.
observations.recommendation:
Management should review and realign the organisational structure to ensure independence of the Risk Management function by:

- Revising the reporting line of the Head of Risk to a more independent governance authority (CEO/MD and Board Risk Committee).

Thereby, clearly separating the Risk function from business generation and credit operations.

- Communicate the change to all relevant stakeholders (HoR, and Executive Management)
observations.managementResponse: This was corrected in the new HR policy. The updated organogram in the recently Board approved HR manual reflects the correct structure.

observations.title: Absence of Customer Complaints Handling Policy
observations.description:
Absence of Customer Complaints Handling Policy
In line with the Consumer Protection regulatory requirements issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria, financial institutions are required to establish a formal complaints management framework to ensure fair treatment of customers.

The framework is expected to include:
- A documented Customer Complaints Handling Policy
- Processes for receiving, tracking and resolving complaints
- Defined timelines for resolution
- Escalation and reporting procedures

Internal Audit observed that the corporation has several complaint channels, with no centralised documented customer complaints handling framework.
observations.risk:
The absence of a formal complaints handling policy exposes the organisation to:

- Non-compliance with CBN consumer protection requirements
- Poor handling or delayed resolution of customer complaints
- Increased reputational risk
observations.rootCause: The absence of a formal Customer Complaints Handling Policy was primarily due to the organisation being in its early operational stage, during which priority was placed on establishing core business operations and service delivery channels. Consequently, the formalisation and documentation of the customer complaints management framework had not yet been completed
observations.recommendation:
Management should develop and implement a Customer Complaints Handling Policy that includes:

- Standard procedures for receiving and logging complaints
- Defined timelines for resolution
- Escalation and reporting mechanisms
- Periodic reporting of complaints to Senior Management and the Board
observations.managementResponse:
Management  acknowledges the regulatory importance of maintaining a formal Customer Complaints Handling Policy in line with applicable CBN Consumer Protection Regulations and industry best practice.

Management is currently working towards the development and implementation of a comprehensive Customer Complaints Handling and Consumer Protection Framework, including formal complaint management procedures, escalation and resolution protocols, service level timelines, complaint monitoring mechanisms, and governance reporting structures to strengthen the Corporation�s consumer protection framework and ensure alignment with applicable regulatory expectations.

observations.title: Absence of Compliance Training Plan and Annual Training Calendar
observations.description:
Absence of Compliance Training Plan and Annual Training Calendar
In accordance with the Central Bank of Nigeria AML/CFT Regulations for Banks and Other Financial Institutions and the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022, regulated institutions are required to maintain a Compliance Programme that includes:
- Ongoing staff compliance and AML/CFT training
- Periodic awareness programmes for all employees
- Structured training plans tailored to staff roles and risk exposure

Training is a mandatory component of an effective compliance framework.

Internal Audit observed that the organisation does not have a documented Compliance Training Plan or Annual Training Calendar. 
No evidence of planned or scheduled compliance training activities was provided.
observations.risk:
- Weak compliance culture across the organisation
- Increased risk of regulatory sanctions
observations.rootCause: The organisation is currently in its developmental phase, and while compliance awareness activities have been conducted on an ad-hoc basis, a structured and documented Compliance Training Plan and Annual Training Calendar had not yet been formally developed and implemented.
observations.recommendation:
Management should develop and implement a Compliance Training Programme that includes:

- A documented annual compliance training plan and calendar.
- Mandatory training for all staff on key regulations.
- Role-based training for high-risk and customer-facing functions.
- Maintenance of training attendance records.
observations.managementResponse: The Corporation has an established Compliance Training & Awareness Framework documented under Appendix 9 of the Board-approved Internal Control & Compliance Policy. The framework outlines the Corporation�s Annual Training & Awareness Calendar, including defined compliance training programmes, target audiences, and implementation timelines covering key regulatory and compliance areas such as AML/CFT/CPF, KYC, ethics, data privacy, cybersecurity, and business continuity.The implementation of the calender has commenced

observations.title: Absence of Data Inventory / Data Mapping Register
observations.description:
Absence of Data Inventory / Data Mapping Register
In accordance with the Nigeria Data Protection regulatory framework issued by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, organisations are required to maintain records of personal data processing activities, including:
- Categories of personal data collected
- Purpose of processing
- Data subjects and data flows
- Data storage and retention
- Third-party data sharing

Maintaining a Data Inventory / Data Mapping Register is a foundational requirement for effective data protection and privacy compliance.

Internal Audit observed that the corporation does not maintain a Data Inventory or Data Mapping Register. No documented record of personal data processing activities was provided for review.
observations.risk:
- Inability to demonstrate compliance with data protection regulations
- Weak visibility over personal data collected and processed
- Increased risk of data breaches and improper data handling
observations.rootCause: The organisation�s data governance and privacy compliance framework is still being developed as part of the broader institutional setup process. As a result, a formal Data Inventory/Data Mapping Register documenting personal data processing activities had not yet been established
observations.recommendation:
Establish a Data Inventory and Data Mapping Register that captures:
- Categories of personal data processed
- Purpose and lawful basis for processing
- Data flows and storage locations
- Third-party data sharing arrangements
- Data retention periods
observations.managementResponse:
Management notes the observation. While the Risk Management & Compliance Department provides regulatory oversight and monitoring responsibilities in respect of data protection and privacy compliance, the operational responsibility for maintaining enterprise-wide Data Inventory and Data Mapping Registers primarily resides with the Information Technology/Data Governance function as custodian of the Corporation�s systems, applications, and data architecture.

Management is currently engaging Executive Management on the urgent need to expedite ongoing efforts towards strengthening the Corporation�s enterprise data governance framework, including the development and implementation of a comprehensive Data Inventory and Data Mapping Register aligned with NDPA/NDPR requirements, ISO 27001 principles, and applicable CBN expectations..

observations.title: Inconsistent Disclosure of Risk Management Policies in the Financial Statements
observations.description:
Inconsistent Disclosure of Risk Management Policies in the Financial Statements
Financial institutions are required to provide adequate disclosures on risk management in their financial statements in accordance with applicable financial reporting standards (including IFRS) and regulatory expectations issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria.

Specifically, Financial Institutions are required to disclose a summary of their risk management policies and framework, reflecting the nature and extent of risks arising from their operations and the controls in place to manage those risks.

Internal Audit observed that the risk management disclosures in the corporation�s financial statements:
- Do not accurately reflect the existing risk management and control environment
- Provide limited or generic information on risk governance structures and controls
- Do not fully describe the key risk management policies currently in operation
observations.risk:
Inadequate disclosure of risk management policies may result in:

- Misrepresentation of the corporation�s risk profile to stakeholders
- Reduced transparency in financial reporting
- Regulatory concerns during supervisory review
- Reputational risk and loss of stakeholder confidence
observations.rootCause: No process for review of audited financial statements by risk management and company secretariat before finalization.
observations.recommendation:
Management should:

- Ensure alignment between internal risk governance documentation and external financial reporting.
- Involve Risk, Finance, and Legal functions in the review of annual disclosures prior to publication.
observations.managementResponse: The Finance Department is currently awaiting feedback from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) on the 2025 financial statements review. Upon receipt, we will incorporate the Risk Department�s input on risk management disclosures to ensure they are accurate, comprehensive, and aligned with regulatory requirements.

observations.title: Inconsistencies in Regulatory Classification and Misstatement of Corporate Information Across Official Records and Financial Statements
observations.description:
Inconsistencies in Regulatory Classification and Misstatement of Corporate Information Across Official Records and Financial Statements
Regulated financial institutions are required to ensure consistency and accuracy in all official disclosures. These records must consistently reflect the institution�s true legal status and permitted business activities.

Internal Audit observed inconsistencies in the corporation�s regulatory and financial reporting disclosures as follows:
- The CAC Status Report describes the organisation�s principal activity as micro-lending.
- The organisation�s CBN license classifies it as a Wholesale Development Finance Institution (DFI).
- The audited financial statements incorrectly describe the institution as a commercial bank engaged in retail and consumer banking activities.

These inconsistencies indicate a misalignment between corporate registration, regulatory licensing, and financial reporting disclosures.
observations.risk:
These inconsistencies expose the organisation to significant regulatory and governance risks, including:

- Misrepresentation of the institution�s regulatory status and licensed activities
- Potential breach and supervisory action
- Loss of credibility of audited financial statements
observations.rootCause: Oversight
observations.recommendation:
Management should:
- Reconcile and align all regulatory and statutory records
- Correct the misstatement in the audited financial statements to reflect the accurate regulatory classification (Wholesale DFI).
- Ensure annual validation of all external disclosures prior to issuance of financial statements.
observations.managementResponse:
The Finance Department is currently awaiting feedback from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) on the 2025 financial statements review. Upon receipt of this feedback, we will proceed to formally restate Credicorp�s object clause to align with its mandate as a Wholesale Development Finance Institution (DFI).

The CSLA also noted that discussions are ongoing to correct the principal activity on the status report.

observations.title: Outdated Directors� Information in Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) Records
observations.description:
Outdated Directors� Information in CAC Records
In accordance with statutory corporate governance requirements under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) and regulatory expectations, regulated institutions are required to maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date records of their Board of Directors with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC).

Changes in Board composition (appointments, resignations, or removals) must be promptly updated in statutory filings to ensure legal and regulatory accuracy.

Internal Audit observed discrepancies between the organisation�s actual Board composition and CAC records:
- Some directors who have resigned are still reflected as active directors in the CAC status report. 
- Some directors who have been formally inaugurated are not reflected in the CAC records.
observations.risk:
This inconsistency exposes the organisation to significant risks, including:

- Legal uncertainty regarding the validity of Board decisions made by incorrectly recorded directors
- Non-compliance with statutory CAMA filing requirements
- Regulatory concerns during supervisory or due diligence reviews
observations.rootCause: These vacancies were recently approved at the last board meeting
observations.recommendation: Update CAC records to reflect the current and accurate Board composition.
observations.managementResponse: The approval of the Board to fill casual vacancies of 2 directors following their resignation, was recently obtained at the last Board meeting, and the Resolution will be filed shortly at the CAC following which it will reflect on the CAC 7.�

observations.title: Absence of Appointment of AML/CFT Compliance Officer
observations.description:
Absence of Appointment of AML/CFT Compliance Officer
In accordance with the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022 and the AML/CFT Regulations issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria, regulated financial institutions are required to appoint a designated AML/CFT Compliance Officer (Money Laundering Reporting Officer � MLRO).

The appointed officer is responsible for:
- Implementing AML/CFT compliance programmes
- Monitoring suspicious transactions
- Filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) and Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs)
- Ensuring staff AML/CFT training and awareness
- Serving as the primary liaison with regulatory authorities

Internal Audit did not obtain evidence of the appointment of a designated AML/CFT Compliance Officer (MLRO) for the corporation.
No formal appointment letter or designation document was provided for review.
observations.risk:
- Non-compliance with statutory AML/CFT requirements
- No accountability for AML/CFT implementation
observations.rootCause: The absence of a formally designated AML/CFT Compliance Officer was due to the organisation still being in its early operational and governance structuring phase. While certain AML/CFT responsibilities were being performed within the Compliance function, formal designation and documentation of the MLRO role had not yet been concluded.
observations.recommendation:
- Appoint a qualified AML/CFT Compliance Officer (MLRO) in writing.
Clearly define the officer�s roles, responsibilities, and reporting line.
- Ensure the AML/CFT Officer has independence and direct access to senior management and the Board.
- Update the AML/CFT policy to reflect the appointment.
observations.managementResponse:
Management acknowledges the regulatory requirement for the formal designation of an AML/CFT Compliance Officer in line with applicable CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations and extant anti-money laundering laws and guidelines.
AML/CFT compliance oversight responsibilities are currently being performed within the Risk Management & Compliance function and management is taking steps to formally designate and operationalize the role of an AML/CFT Compliance Officer with clearly defined responsibilities and governance authority in alignment with regulatory requirements and industry best practice.

observations.title: Expenses Not Accrued in the Correct Financial Period (Unrecorded Liabilities)
observations.description:
Expenses Not Accrued in the Correct Financial Period (Unrecorded Liabilities)
During the review of expense and procurement transactions, we identified invoices relating to goods/services received in the 2025 financial year that were only recorded as expenses in 2026. No accruals were raised at year-end to recognise these costs in the correct accounting period.

Examples:
1. Vendor payments for 10,000 women in mobility event which took place in 2025. The related expenses were first recognised in 2026.
2. Programme support services related to YouthCred. The YouthCred launch happened in 2025, however, the expenses were recognised in the following year.
3. Benarc Construction office expansion shows that the works were done in 2025, hence the invoice raised, however, this was only recognised in 2026.
observations.risk:
- Understatement of expenses and overstatement of profit in 2025
- Overstatement of expenses in 2026
- Non-compliance with applicable accounting standards and internal financial reporting policies.
observations.rootCause: The information about the transactions was unknown to the finance team in the relevant FY
observations.recommendation:
a) Management should implement a formal month-end and year-end accrual process requiring all departments to identify goods and services received but not yet invoiced. 
b) A standard cut-off checklist and review process should be introduced to ensure expenses are recognised in the correct accounting period before financial close.
observations.managementResponse: The accruals for the transactions were not made because the department didn�t receive any formal information concerning the cost as at end of the period under review.

observations.title: Misclassification of Expenses to Incorrect General Ledger Accounts
observations.description:
Misclassification of Expenses to Incorrect General Ledger Accounts
During the review of expense transactions, we observed instances where costs were recorded in inappropriate general ledger accounts. For example:

1. Event-related expenses (e.g., hall arrangements) were posted to the Branding/Sensitisation GL.

2. Facility management expenses were posted to the Training Cost GL.

3. ECL Model Development Services posted to IT license and subscriptions and not consulting fees or professional services

These expenses were not recorded in accounts that reflect their true nature.
observations.risk:
Incorrect expense classification may result in:

- Inaccurate financial and management reporting
- Distortion of budgets reports & decisions
- Potential misinterpretation during external audits or oversight reviews.
observations.rootCause: Oversight
observations.recommendation:
a) Management should reinforce review controls over expense postings and provide clear guidance on the use of general ledger accounts. 
b) A periodic review of expense classifications should be performed to identify and correct mispostings, and staff responsible for processing expenses should receive refresher training on the chart of accounts.
c) The need for reclassification should be assessed and necessary action taken after a wholistic review by management on the impact of the misclassifications identified in (b) above.
observations.managementResponse:
The reclassification of the ECL model has been effected. 

While we are working on the Facility Expense

The classification of events is posted to Branding/Sensitisation GL.

observations.title: User Access Granted Without Approved Access Request Forms
observations.description:
User Access Granted Without Approved Access Request Forms
During the review of user access management, we observed that access rights for staff configured on the application were not supported by approved user access request forms. Evidence of formal authorisation prior to granting system access was not available.

In addition, we noted two (2) privileged generic accounts, whose access and ownership have not been documented and approved. For effective management and in accordance with information security practices, these access should be deactivated where possible.

Where a deactivation is impracticable or their use is unavoidable, strong compensating controls should be implemented.
observations.risk: The use of privileged generic accounts weakens accountability and increases the risk of unauthorized or fraudulent system activities.
observations.rootCause: Ongoing dependence on consultants for integration with other accounts.
observations.recommendation:
a) Management should enforce a formal user access management process requiring documented and approved access request forms before system access is granted. 
b) Periodic access reviews should also be implemented to ensure all active users have valid and approved access rights.
c) For effective management and in accordance with information security practices, the priviledged generic accounts should be deactivated where possible. Where a deactivation is impracticable or their use is unavoidable, strong compensating controls should be implemented.
observations.managementResponse:
We engaged with the finance and IT team and noted that the priviledged access is with the vendors. They noted that the access has been retained temporarily to support the implementation of a middleware.

Audit Comment: Despite the case by management above, no formally documented risk assessment and approval exist for this privileged account.

observations.title: Underpayment Risk Due to Incorrect Stamp Duty Computation on Outsourcing Contract
observations.description:
Underpayment Risk Due to Incorrect Stamp Duty Computation on Outsourcing Contract
During the review of the CEONEL outsourcing contract, we noted that stamp duty was calculated based only on the management fee component of the contract. The computation did not include the full contract consideration, which also comprises payments made to the outsourced agents.
observations.risk: Incorrect computation of stamp duty exposes the organisation to risk of statutory non-compliance.
observations.rootCause: Oversight
observations.recommendation: Management should perform a comprehensive review of the stamp duty treatment of all existing contracts to ensure duty is calculated on the full consideration in line with applicable regulations. The team should obtain guidiance from the corporation's tax consultants where necessary and implement a review control to ensure correct statutory deductions for all future contracts.
observations.managementResponse:
We engaged with the finance team who averred that this was an oversight and an isolated issue.

They confirmed that stamp duty is computed on the full contract amount and care will be taken to ensure compliance going forward.

The financial impact of the error is ~40,000.

observations.title: Inadequate Verification of Travel Vendor Invoices
observations.description:
Inadequate Verification of Travel Vendor Invoices
During the review of travel expenses, we noted that the travel vendor submits monthly invoices detailing flight bookings and related costs. However, there is no evidence of an independent verification process to confirm that the ticket prices billed align with actual market or airline prices at the time of booking.
observations.risk:
Lack of independent validation of travel costs exposes the organisation to:

- Risk of overbilling or inflated ticket prices
- Financial loss due to weak price assurance controls
- Increased reliance on vendor representations without verification.
observations.rootCause: Over-reliance on third-party travel consultant
observations.recommendation: Management should implement a process to independently verify travel vendor invoices before payment. This may include reviewing booking confirmations, airline receipts, or performing periodic price benchmarking checks. Supporting documentation should be retained to demonstrate that billed travel costs are accurate and reasonable.
observations.managementResponse: The admin team noted the recommendation and averred that they have informed the vendor to include the tickets (with the costs contained on the attached tickets), when submitting their invoices.

observations.title: Expense Journals Posted on Net Basis Without Recognition of Statutory Deductions
observations.description:
Expense Journals Posted on Net Basis Without Recognition of Statutory Deductions
During the review of expense journals in the EasyBank system, we observed that several vendor payments were recorded on a net basis. The related journals did not reflect the gross expense amount, therefore, we were unable to identify the tax deductions for the accounts. 

Examples: 
- 1 April 2026 Payment for Internet Services at the Office (March- April 2026)- 13th 1,520,000

- 23 March 2026 Payment for Q1 Stakeholder Engagement Forum in Abuja-X O int'l Events 2,484,226.25

- 23 March 2026 Payment for Q1 Stakeholder Engagement Forum in Lagos-X O int'l Events 2,517,500

- 19 February 2026 Payment for 2026 IT Reimbursables - 6 months Microsoft Office 18,513,600

- 25 February 2026 Payment for Board Induction and Training Activities 26,185,646.55

- 18 February 2026 Payment for Venue Securing upcoming CREDICORP Board meeting 6,530,000
observations.risk:
Recording expenses on a net basis exposes the organisation to:

Understatement of expenses and liabilities in the financial statements
Risk of non-compliance with statutory tax deduction and remittance requirements
Potential penalties, interest, and additional tax assessments
Inaccurate financial and management reporting due to incomplete recording of transactions.
observations.rootCause: Net basis of posting of transactions causing the omission.
observations.recommendation: Management should ensure all vendor payments are recorded at gross value in the general ledger, with corresponding recognition of VAT and Withholding Tax liabilities where applicable. A review control should be implemented to verify proper accounting treatment of statutory deductions before journal posting.
observations.managementResponse:
The finance team noted these issues and have now reversed and reposted the transactions to provide for the provisions.

During a further discussion, we reiterated the need to ensure adequate posting of transactions to properly account for the expenses and resulting statutory deductions.

We also reiterated the need for adequate review of ledger entries before approving for posting as a preventive measure.

observations.title: Payment Made Without Supporting Evidence and Via Staff Personal Account
observations.description:
Payment Made Without Supporting Evidence and Via Staff Personal Account
During the review of expenses, we observed some expense payments made directly to staff accounts. No evidence of re-confirmation of on-payment to vendor was obtained. 

While approval for the expense was sighted, no receipt, invoice, or other evidence was available to confirm that the service was actually procured/paid for. 

Examples:
- Payment for IT reimbursables. 
- Purchase of a six-month subscription (Zoho for 25 users).
observations.risk:
This practice exposes the organisation to significant risks, including:

Risk of fraud or misappropriation of funds
Inability to confirm that goods/services were received
Weak audit trail and poor accountability for expenditure
Risk of duplicate or unauthorised payments
Potential reputational and regulatory concerns regarding financial governance.
observations.rootCause: Weak expense processing controls
observations.recommendation: Management should enforce a policy requiring that all payments be supported by valid invoices/receipts and be made directly to approved vendors or service providers. The use of staff personal accounts for official transactions should be prohibited except under formally approved petty cash or reimbursement procedures, with full supporting documentation and post-payment verification.
observations.managementResponse:
We discussed this with the team and the third-party invoices are being gathered.

They have noted that going forward this will be strictly enforced to facilitate validation of expense amounts.

observations.title: Inaccurate Transaction Narration Affecting Audit Trail and Traceability
observations.description:
Inaccurate Transaction Narration Affecting Audit Trail and Traceability
During the review of selected expense transactions, we observed an instance where the transaction narration recorded in the accounting system did not accurately reflect the nature of the underlying expense. This inconsistency made it difficult to efficiently trace and match the transaction to its corresponding supporting documentation and source records.

- 19 February 2026 Payment for additional 400L of Diesel - Feb 2026 502,500
observations.risk:
- Difficulty in tracing transactions to supporting documentation
- Increased audit effort and reduced audit efficiency
- Weak audit trail integrity and reduced transparency
- Risk of misclassification or concealment of transactions
- Reduced reliability of financial records for reporting and review purposes
observations.rootCause: Oversight
observations.recommendation: The supervisory review control should be enforced to ensure that transaction descriptions and accounts are validated before posting.
observations.managementResponse:
We discussed with the finance team and noted that this was an oversight. This has now been corrected by the team. 

We also reiterated the need for adequate review of ledger entries before approving for posting as a preventive measure.

observations.title: Award Letter and Payment Without Signed Contract
observations.description:
Award Letter and Payment Without Signed Contract
An instance was identified where an award letter and payment existed without an executed/signed contract. (BMT - two awards granted in December 2024 , N247,250,000 and N247,250,000)
observations.risk:
This exposes the corporation to:
- Legal and contractual disputes
- Unclear deliverables and service scope
- Non-compliance with procurement and governance policies
observations.rootCause: Oversight. Legacy transactions
observations.recommendation: Management should enforce strict adherence to procurement procedures by ensuring that signed contracts are in place before any payment is made.
observations.managementResponse:
The Legal Department has been engaged to properly document the contract based on the award letters.

Update: This has now been remediated. 

The procurement team averred that controls have now been implemented to prevent such recurrence.

audits.name: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Audit - Q2

reports.title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Audit - Q2

observations.title: Non-Implementation of Approved Business Continuity Policy.
observations.description:
Non-Implementation of Approved Business Continuity Policy. 
The Corporation has an approved Business Continuity Policy; however, there was no evidence of effective implementation across business units during the audit period. There was no evidence of an approved BC/DR Testing and Exercise Schedule showing the operationalization of the BCMS.
observations.risk: Inability to effectively activate business continuity arrangements during disruption events, resulting in prolonged downtime of critical operations, potential regulatory non-compliance, and increased operational and reputational risk.
observations.rootCause: Weak enforcement of policy requirements and lack of clear accountability for implementation across business units.
observations.recommendation: Management should ensure full implementation of the approved Business Continuity Policy across all business units, with clearly assigned ownership, defined implementation timelines, and periodic monitoring to confirm compliance and operationalization.
observations.managementResponse:
The BCM Policy was developed to establish the Corporation's governance framework and minimum requirements for business continuity. Its implementation will be undertaken as a phased programme to ensure the structured development of key BCM components, including governance structures, Business Impact Analysis (BIA), Business Continuity Plans (BCPs), Disaster Recovery (DR) arrangements, training, and testing.

Implementation will commence in Q3 2026 beginning with the establishment of the BCM governance structure, Business Continuity Management Team (BCMT), and other foundational documentation, including the BCM Implementation Roadmap. The BC/DR Testing and Exercise Schedule will then be developed and approved, following which periodic tabletop exercises, disaster recovery tests, evacuation drills, and enterprise-wide simulation exercises will be conducted in accordance with the approved schedule.

observations.title: Absence of Business Continuity Training and Awareness Programme.
observations.description:
Absence of Business Continuity Training and Awareness Programme.
Audit observed that there is no structured or consistent Business Continuity training and awareness programme across the Corporation. Staff have not been formally trained on their roles and responsibilities under the Business Continuity Plan, and awareness of incident response procedures, escalation paths, and recovery expectations remains limited.
observations.risk: This increases the risk of ineffective response during disruption events, as staff may be unable to execute assigned continuity roles. This may lead to delayed recovery, operational inefficiencies, increased downtime, and potential regulatory non-compliance during crisis.
observations.rootCause: Absence of a formal BCM training framework and lack of defined training schedules and ownership for continuous awareness delivery.
observations.recommendation: Management should implement a structured Business Continuity training and awareness programme, ensuring role-based training, periodic refresher sessions, and documented evidence of staff participation to strengthen organisational preparedness.
observations.managementResponse:
This observation is attributable to the proposed phased implementation of the Corporation's Business Continuity Management (BCM) framework, with initial efforts focused on establishing the governance framework through the approval of the BCM Policy.

A structured BCM training and awareness programme will commence in Q3 2026, incorporating staff awareness sessions, role-based training, executive and Board briefings, and simulation exercises. BCM training will thereafter form part of the Corporation's annual training calendar, supported by periodic refresher programmes to strengthen organisational resilience and preparedness.

observations.title: Absence of Crisis Management and Crisis Communication Plans.
observations.description:
Absence of Crisis Management and Crisis Communication Plans.
The Corporation does not have a formally documented Crisis Management Plan or Crisis Communication Plan. While general BCM and DR documentation exists, there are no clearly defined procedures for crisis leadership structure, decision-making authority, stakeholder communication, or external/internal communication during disruptive events.
observations.risk: Lack of structured crisis coordination and communication may result in delayed decision-making, inconsistent messaging to stakeholders, reputational damage, regulatory scrutiny, and ineffective management of operational disruptions during major incidents.
observations.rootCause: inadequate framework development and insufficient integration of crisis management requirements within the BCM framework.
observations.recommendation: Management should develop and approve a formal Crisis Management Plan and Crisis Communication Plan, clearly defining governance structure, escalation pathways, communication protocols, and roles/responsibilities. These plans should be integrated into the broader BCM framework and tested periodically.
observations.managementResponse:
This will form part of the BCM implementation roadmap. Dedicated Crisis Management and Crisis Communication Plans will be developed from Q3 2026 to establish the crisis governance structure, define roles and decision-making authority, and document escalation procedures and internal and external stakeholder communication protocols.

The plans will be periodically tested through simulation exercises to validate their effectiveness and strengthen the Corporation's crisis response and communication readiness.

observations.title: Inadequate Disaster Recovery Infrastructure and Absence of DR Testing.
observations.description:
Inadequate Disaster Recovery Infrastructure and Absence of DR Testing.
The Corporation maintains data backup processes; however, there is no fully established disaster recovery infrastructure to support system recovery and business resumption in the event of a major disruption. In addition, no disaster recovery testing has been conducted to validate the effectiveness of recovery arrangements, despite the existence of backup solutions.
observations.risk: Inability to restore critical systems within acceptable recovery timeframes during a major disruption, leading to extended service downtime, data integrity risks, operational losses, regulatory exposure, and reputational damage.
observations.rootCause: Weak DR architecture design and absence of a structured DR testing program to validate recovery capability and readiness.
observations.recommendation: Management should establish a formal disaster recovery infrastructure aligned with defined RTO/RPO requirements and implement a structured DR testing program, including periodic end-to-end recovery and failover/failback simulations to validate readiness.

observations.title: Weak Third-Party Resilience Monitoring.
observations.description:
Weak Third-Party Resilience Monitoring.  
The Corporation relies on critical third-party service providers for key operational and technology services; however, there is limited evidence of structured assessment and ongoing monitoring of their business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities. Vendor resilience assurances, where obtained, are not consistently updated or independently validated.
observations.risk: Exposure to service disruptions originating from third-party failures, leading to potential downtime of critical services, operational interruptions, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational damage due to inability to maintain service continuity.
observations.rootCause: Inadequate third-party risk management framework integration with BCM/DR requirements and insufficient ongoing vendor resilience oversight.
observations.recommendation: Management should strengthen third-party resilience monitoring by implementing periodic vendor BCM/DR assessments, requiring evidence of recovery testing from critical providers, and embedding resilience requirements within contractual agreements and SLA frameworks.

observations.title: Weak Contractual Governance Over Software Defined Data Center (SDDC) Arrangement.
observations.description:
Weak Contractual Governance Over Software Defined Data Center (SDDC) Arrangement.
The Corporation does not have a direct or tri-partite contractual agreement governing the Software Defined Data Center (SDDC) arrangement. The SDDC consultant is engaged indirectly through another consultant on behalf of the Corporation; however, this engagement structure is not clearly defined or formally documented within existing contractual agreements.
observations.risk: Lack of clearly defined contractual relationships exposes the Bank to governance ambiguity, limited enforceability of service obligations, increased operational and legal risk, and potential challenges in accountability during service failures or disputes.
observations.rootCause: Inadequate contract structuring and insufficient legal/third-party governance review during engagement setup for critical infrastructure services.
observations.recommendation: Management should formalize a direct or tri-partite agreement for the SDDC arrangement, clearly defining roles, responsibilities, service obligations, accountability lines, and performance expectations. Legal and procurement functions should review and standardize all critical infrastructure engagements to ensure enforceable governance structures are in place.

observations.title: Generic IT Disaster Recovery Plan
observations.description:
Generic IT Disaster Recovery Plan
The IT Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) v1.0 defines Recovery Time Objective (RTO) tiers (Tier 1: 0�4 hours; Tier 2: 4�24 hours; Tier 3: 24�72 hours) and references backup types and a general recovery workflow. However, the Plan does not include a system/application inventory mapped to these tiers, does not specify a designated DR site or failover infrastructure, omits backup control parameters (retention periods, storage locations, encryption, immutability), contains no evidence or schedule of DR testing, and does not name individuals, deputies, or a formal disaster-declaration authority within the roles defined in Section 5.0. The document is also unsigned, with the "Approved By" and "Effective Date" fields blank
observations.risk: Without this detail, the stated RTOs and RPOs are unverifiable commitments rather than achievable, control-backed targets. In the event of an actual disruption, the organization has no assurance that systems can be restored within the stated timeframes, that backups are recoverable, intact, or protected from ransomware, or that recovery activities will be coordinated under clear authority.
observations.rootCause: The Disaster Recovery Plan was developed at a high level without a comprehensive disaster recovery governance process, resulting in the omission of critical recovery, testing, backup, ownership, and approval requirements.
observations.recommendation: Management should update and formally approve the Disaster Recovery Plan to include system-to-RTO mapping, DR site and failover arrangements, backup control requirements, recovery roles and responsibilities, disaster recovery testing procedures, and periodic review mechanisms to ensure effective recovery during disruptions.

observations.title: Weaknesses in Loan Disbursement Controls and Documentation
observations.description:
Weaknesses in Loan Disbursement Controls and Documentation:
No Legal Documentation for Disbursement. In certain instances, loan facilities were disbursed without complete legal documentation. Specifically, legal documentation for the following disbursements were not sighted: Credit Direct � 1.5b, 4.5b
Disbursement of Loan Not in Line with Documented Contract. We also observed an instance where loan disbursements were not executed in accordance with approved contractual terms. (Ecobank disbursement of 1b requiring 20.5% for tenors greater than 3 years, however, 50m from that disbursement was offered at 15%)

observations.title: Subscription Management � Multiple FortiGuard Subscriptions Expired
observations.description:
Subscription Management � Multiple FortiGuard Subscriptions Expired
Five key security subscriptions that allow the firewall to identify and block current threats expired on 4 February 2026. These are: Firmware & General Updates, Intrusion Prevention (IPS), AntiVirus, Web Filtering, and Outbreak Prevention. Two additional services � FortiGate Cloud and SD-WAN Network Monitor � are also unlicensed. Without these active subscriptions, the firewall is running on outdated threat intelligence and cannot defend against attacks discovered after 4 Feb 2026.
observations.risk: The firewall is like a security guard who has not received any briefings since February 2026 � it cannot recognise any new threats since that date. Malware, ransomware, phishing sites, and network exploits that emerged after 4 Feb 2026 will pass through unchallenged. The Antivirus and Intrusion Prevention profiles shown as 'active' in the firewall policy are effectively inactive because their signature databases are frozen. CREDICORP is exposed to the full spectrum of modern threats without the detection tools needed to stop them.
observations.rootCause: Five FortiGuard security subscriptions expired as of 4 February 2026: Firmware & General Updates, Intrusion Prevention (IPS), AntiVirus, Web Filtering, and Outbreak Prevention. FortiGate Cloud and SD-WAN Network Monitor are also unlicensed.
observations.recommendation:
1. Immediately renew all five expired FortiGuard subscriptions: Firmware & General Updates, IPS, AntiVirus, Web Filtering, and Outbreak Prevention.
2. Assign P1 (highest priority) budget allocation for renewal � this is not discretionary.
3. Assess whether FortiGate Cloud and SD-WAN Network Monitor licences are operationally required and procure if so.
4. After renewal, confirm signature databases update successfully before relying on AV/IPS controls.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: Internal

Management acknowledges the observation. The procurement process for the renewal of the required security subscriptions and service contracts is currently in progress. Completion of the renewals is expected by the end of April 2026.

observations.title: Publicly Exposed Management Interface
observations.description:
Publicly Exposed Management Interface 
The firewall's administration login page is directly accessible from the public internet. several failed login attempts were recorded from different different IP addresses in just 21 hours  an organised, coordinated attack is actively underway. Attackers are using known FortiGate account names, showing they have already identified the device type. The DMZ interface (a semi-trusted network zone) also has management access enabled, which is against security best practice.
observations.risk: CREDICORP's firewall administration panel is visible and accessible to anyone on the internet, and a professional attack campaign is already attempting to break in. If a single username and password combination is guessed correctly, attackers gain complete control over the organisation's network perimeter. There are no additional barriers (e.g., multi-factor authentication or IP restrictions) to stop them once the password is compromised. This is not a potential future risk � an attack is in progress right now.
observations.rootCause: WAN interfaces (wan1: 160.119.124.76, wan2: 41.242.56.148) have HTTP, HTTPS, and PING enabled as admin access protocols. DMZ interface (10.10.10.1/24) also has PING and HTTPS management enabled.
observations.recommendation:
1. Disable HTTP, HTTPS, and Ping management access on both public-facing (WAN) interfaces. Disable HTTPS and Ping on the DMZ interface.
2. Restrict all management access to a dedicated internal management network � administrators should connect via VPN first, then manage the firewall from inside.
3. Block the top attacking IP subnets at the firewall policy level.
4. Strengthen the lockout settings: ban IPs for 1 hour after 3 failed attempts.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The public accessibility of the firewall administration interface was intentionally enabled to facilitate remote support by the external service provider (IBIS) where required. This decision was taken as a temporary risk-based measure to ensure operational support continuity.

The recommendation for the implementation of secure VPN-based administrative access, including the required cost assessment will be evaluated. 

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.title: Super Admin Account Without MFA
observations.description:
Super Admin Account Without MFA 
The most powerful administrator account ('admin') has no second-factor authentication and no IP address restrictions. Within 21 hours, this account logged in successfully 17 times from 6 different external IP addresses � with no MFA challenge at any point.
observations.risk: The combination of no MFA and no IP restrictions means the firewall's highest-privilege account can be accessed from anywhere in the world with just a password.
observations.rootCause: admin' account (super_admin profile): 2FA disabled, no Trusted Hosts configured. Account authenticated 17 times from 6 different external IPs in 21 hours. .
observations.recommendation:
1.  Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA/FortiToken) on the 'admin' account.
2.  Configure Trusted Host restrictions � limit login to known management IP addresses only.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The current configuration was implemented to enable timely remote support by the external service provider (IBIS), as the administrative support resources are not located on-site. This was accepted as a temporary, risk-based arrangement to maintain operational continuity.

An evaluation of the recommendations including the potential operational and cost implications will be assessed and communicated to the team by the timeline. 

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.title: Permissive Outbound Policy � No Segmentation, No Application Control
observations.description:
Permissive Outbound Policy � No Segmentation, No Application Control
The entire internal-to-internet firewall ruleset consists of a single rule: allow everything from everyone to everywhere, at all times. All internal devices � workstations, servers, payment systems � sit on the same flat network with no separation, and any of them can reach any internet destination on any port or protocol. This rule has processed 61.61 GB of traffic with no application visibility or URL filtering in place.
observations.risk: Without outbound traffic controls, CREDICORP has no technical barrier preventing: staff uploading sensitive data to personal cloud services; malware on any internal PC 'phoning home' to attacker-controlled servers; employees accessing gambling, malware-hosting, or inappropriate websites; and data exfiltration using any protocol. The 61 GB of outbound traffic recorded has no record of where it went or what it contained � CREDICORP cannot determine if any data has already left the organisation through this gap.
observations.rootCause: Single outbound rule 'Lan_To_Internet': Source=all, Destination=all, Service=ALL, Action=ACCEPT, Schedule=always. Flat LAN (10.10.11.0/24) � internal1�5 ports all in single VLAN, no zone separation. No Application Control profile. No Web Filter profile. AV and IPS profiles applied but cannot compensate for absence of access control policy. Policy has processed 61.61 GB traffic.
observations.recommendation:
1. Replace the single any-to-any rule with specific rules for defined business functions (e.g., web browsing, email, payment systems).
2. Implement Web Filtering to block malicious and non-business-appropriate sites.
3.Implement Application Control to prevent unauthorised application traffic.
4.Separate the internal network into zones: User, Server, and Management VLANs.
5.Apply least-privilege principles: each zone should only be permitted the traffic necessary for its specific function.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS & Internal

The current firewall configuration reflects the organisation�s existing flat network architecture and was implemented to maintain operational continuity.

The development and approval of the relevant network security policies and standards will be prioritised to enable the implementation of appropriate firewall rules and segmentation.

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.title: Password Policy Disabled � No Complexity, Length, or Expiry Requirements
observations.description: The firewall's built-in password policy is turned off. There are no enforced requirements for minimum password length, complexity (e.g., mix of uppercase, numbers, and symbols), or expiration for any administrator account. The highest-privilege account on the device could theoretically have a very short or simple password with no technical control preventing this.
observations.risk: With an active brute-force campaign of over 51,000 attempts underway, the strength of the admin password is a critical line of defence. A weak or short password is far more likely to be guessed, especially in a distributed attack from 108 IP addresses. Without password expiry, a compromised password would remain valid indefinitely. This gap directly compounds the risk from Finding 1 (exposed management interface) and Finding 2 (no MFA).
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 5): Password scope = 'Off'. No minimum length, complexity, or expiry enforced for any admin account. super_admin 'admin' account therefore protected only by password of unknown strength.
observations.recommendation:
1. Enable the Password Policy: System > Settings > Password Policy � set scope to 'Both'.
2. Set minimum password length to 12 characters.
3. Require complexity: uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The firewall password policy will be configured and enforced immediately to ensure appropriate password complexity, minimum length, and other relevant security requirements.

Timeline: 1 week

observations.title: Telnet Administrative Service Configured � Unencrypted Management Protocol
observations.description: Telnet is configured as an available administrative service on the firewall. Telnet is an obsolete protocol that transmits all communication � including usernames, passwords, and all commands � in plain, unencrypted text across the network. It was superseded by SSH (Secure Shell) over 25 years ago and should not be present on any production security device.
observations.risk: Any network monitoring tool or attacker positioned on the same network path can capture and read all Telnet traffic in real time � including admin credentials. On a firewall that is already under active brute-force attack, exposing any plaintext authentication channel is unacceptable. Telnet has no legitimate modern use case on a security device when SSH is available.
observations.rootCause: Telnet configured as administrative service on the FortiGate. Telnet transmits all data including credentials in unencrypted plaintext over the network. No legitimate use case on a production security device when SSH is available.
observations.recommendation:
1. Disable Telnet immediately via CLI: config system global > set admin-telnet disable > end.
2. Verify that SSH (port 22) remains enabled as the sole CLI management protocol.
3. Restrict SSH access to trusted management IP addresses only, consistent with Finding 1 recommendations.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

Telnet is recognised as an insecure and obsolete protocol. Telnet will be disabled immediately, and administrative access will be restricted to secure, encrypted protocols in line with security best practices.

Timeline: 1 week

observations.title: System Timezone Set to Pacific Time � 9-Hour Log Timestamp Error
observations.description: The firewall's system clock is set to GMT-8 (Pacific Time, USA) instead of West Africa Time (WAT, UTC+1), which is the correct timezone for CREDICORP's operations in Nigeria. This means every single log entry on this device has a timestamp that is 9 hours behind actual local time. All 52,816 log entries analysed in this audit carry this incorrect timestamp.
observations.risk: Every security event in this firewall's history has the wrong time recorded. For the potential incident identified in Finding 2, configuration changes logged as occurring in the middle of the night are actually mid-morning business hours � a material difference for investigation purposes. In any regulatory investigation, forensic analysis, or legal proceeding, incorrect timestamps undermine the evidential value of the logs. PCI DSS explicitly requires all system clocks to be correctly synchronised.
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 7): Timezone = GMT-8:00 (Pacific Time, US & Canada). CREDICORP operates in Nigeria under WAT (UTC+1). All 52,816 log entries carry tz='-0700'. Actual WAT time = displayed time + 9 hours.
observations.recommendation:
1. Immediately correct the timezone: System > Settings > Time zone > Africa/Lagos (UTC+1/WAT).
2. Verify NTP synchronisation continues to function correctly after the timezone correction.
3. Document the affected log period in all audit and incident records � all historical logs must have 9 hours added to show the true local time.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

Management acknowledges the observation. The firewall�s system clock will be corrected to West Africa Time (WAT, UTC+1) to ensure that all log entries accurately reflect local time.

observations.title: USB Auto-Install Enabled � Unauthenticated Physical Override
observations.description: The firewall is configured to automatically apply any configuration file or firmware image found on a USB drive inserted into the device � with no password, no MFA, and no administrator approval required. This feature is intended for initial factory deployment of new devices but has not been disabled now that the device is in live production.
observations.risk: Anyone with physical access to the firewall � a cleaning contractor, a disgruntled employee, a courier � could insert a pre-prepared USB drive and completely overwrite the firewall's configuration or firmware in seconds, with no credentials required and potentially no audit trail. For a financial institution's perimeter firewall, this is an unacceptable physical security bypass of all digital access controls. This risk is elevated given the suspected unauthorised access identified in Finding 2.
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 8): USB auto-install enabled for 'Detect configuration' (fgt_system.conf) and 'Detect firmware' (image.out). Insertion of USB containing these filenames applies config/firmware automatically with no GUI/CLI authentication required.
observations.recommendation:
1. Disable USB auto-install immediately: System > Settings > Start Up Settings � set both 'Detect configuration' and 'Detect firmware' toggles to OFF.
2. Review and enforce physical access controls to the network cabinet or server room housing the FortiGate, including access logs and CCTV coverage.
3. Use authenticated methods (FortiManager or TFTP/SCP) for all firmware and configuration management.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The automatic USB-based configuration and firmware update feature will be disabled immediately to prevent unauthorized changes

observations.title: Incomplete Local Traffic Logging and No External Syslog Forwarding
observations.description:
Incomplete Local Traffic Logging and No External Syslog Forwarding
The firewall is not logging allowed or denied network traffic passing through it � only system events (like login attempts) are being recorded. Additionally, no logs are being forwarded to any external system: if the firewall's local log storage is cleared or the device is compromised, all evidence of what occurred is permanently lost. The 61.61 GB of outbound traffic processed has no destination or content record anywhere.
observations.risk: Without traffic logging, CREDICORP cannot determine what data has left the network, which internal devices have made suspicious connections, or whether any malware is communicating with external attacker-controlled servers. In the context of the potential compromise in Finding 2, it is impossible to determine from current logs whether any data was stolen. Without external log forwarding, an attacker who gains firewall access can erase all evidence of their activity.
observations.rootCause: Log & Report Global Settings (Appendix 9): Log allowed traffic = OFF; Log denied unicast = OFF; Log denied broadcast = OFF; Log local out traffic = ON only. Syslog status = Disabled. Event logging = 'All' (source of brute-force and admin event logs analysed in this report). 61.61 GB outbound traffic from Lan_To_Internet has zero session-level log record.
observations.recommendation:
1. Enable 'Log allowed traffic' and 'Log denied unicast traffic' in Log & Report > Global Settings > Local Traffic Logging.
2. Configure Syslog forwarding to an external, dedicated log management server or SIEM solution (e.g., FortiAnalyzer, Splunk, or any RFC 5424-compatible syslog receiver).
3. Set log retention: minimum 90 days online, 12 months archived, per PCI DSS Req. 10.7.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The limited logging is currently due to storage constraints on the firewall. While full logging and forwarding to a centralized security information system (CIS) could be implemented, the immediate cost-benefit may not justify it given the current network architecture.

As an interim measure, a rotational logging mechanism will be explored to capture critical network traffic until a centralized logging solution can be implemented in line with best practices.

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.title: No High Availability � Firewall is a Single Point of Failure
observations.description:
No High Availability � Firewall is a Single Point of Failure
The firewall is operating in 'Standalone' mode with no backup unit configured. There is no automatic failover capability. If this firewall fails � due to hardware fault, power loss, software crash, or even a routine firmware upgrade � all internet-dependent services stop immediately until manual intervention restores the device.
observations.risk: For a financial institution, the firewall is the gateway for payment processing, customer-facing systems, VPN access for remote staff, and email. A single hardware failure causes a complete outage of all these services with no automatic recovery. The ongoing active attack campaign also increases the risk of availability impact from resource exhaustion. This is both a business continuity risk and, for a regulated institution, a potential compliance gap.
observations.rootCause: HA settings (Appenndix 10): Mode = Standalone. No cluster partner configured. Device sustaining 2,986 concurrent sessions and active attack campaign � operating under load with no redundancy.
observations.recommendation:
1. Formally document the single-point-of-failure risk and obtain management sign-off if HA cannot be implemented immediately.
2. Evaluate deploying a second FortiGate 60F in Active-Passive HA mode for automatic failover.
3. At minimum: maintain a current, tested configuration backup stored off-device, and document a hardware replacement procedure with a defined Recovery Time Objective (RTO).
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

Given the current scale of operations, this level of redundancy is considered acceptable.

Management will reassess the need for high-availability and failover capabilities as operational requirements and service dependencies increase.

Timeline: 10 April 2026

observations.title: Auto File System Check Disabled � Silent Corruption Risk
observations.description: A built-in safety feature that checks the firewall's internal file system for errors at startup is turned off. This check is designed to detect and correct file system problems � caused by unexpected power-offs, hardware degradation, or deliberate tampering � before the device comes back online. Without it, file system errors could persist undetected.
observations.risk: A security device with undetected file system corruption may load its configuration incorrectly, have security profiles fail silently, or produce unreliable log files � all without alerting administrators. In the context of the suspected unauthorised access in Finding 2, file system integrity verification is particularly important, as a sophisticated attacker may attempt to modify system files. Silent degradation of a security device is especially dangerous.
observations.rootCause: System Settings (Appendix 8): 'Auto file system check' toggled OFF. Feature performs FortiOS file system integrity validation at boot time, detecting and correcting errors before system online.
observations.recommendation:
1. Enable Auto File System Check: System > Settings > Start Up Settings � toggle 'Auto file system check' to ON.
2. Combine with regular firmware integrity checks and configuration backup verification.
observations.managementResponse:
Response by: IBIS

The firewall�s built-in file system integrity check will be re-enabled.

audits.name: Operational Efficiency and Process Improvement Audit
audits.area: Credit Portfolio, Procurement, Finance, Risk Management

plan.scope: This process audit assesses the operational efficiency and process-improvement maturity of four functions — Credit Portfolio (origination-to-collection lifecycle), Procurement (procure-to-pay), Finance (financial close, payments and reporting) and Risk Management — for the period 1 April to 30 June 2026 (Q2 2026). It focuses on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness (value-for-money) of these processes: cycle times and turnaround, manual effort and automation levels, hand-offs and bottlenecks, rework and error rates, duplication of activity, resource utilisation, SLA/KPI performance, and the extent to which continuous-improvement and data analytics are embedded. It evaluates whether controls are efficient (not just effective) and whether process design supports the Corporation's cost-to-income and service objectives. It does NOT re-perform a full controls-assurance/compliance audit of each function (those are covered by separate risk-based reviews), nor does it cover credit-decision quality, IT general controls, HR/payroll, or strategy formulation, except where these directly affect process efficiency. Absent restriction, the review covers Q2 2026 transactional throughput and process data across the four functions.
objectives: Assess whether key processes in Credit Portfolio, Procurement, Finance and Risk Management operate efficiently — within defined cycle times/SLAs and without avoidable delay, bottlenecks or backlog.
Evaluate the level of manual effort, automation and straight-through processing, and identify opportunities to streamline, automate or eliminate non-value-adding and duplicated activities.
Determine the extent of rework, errors, exceptions and re-processing, and assess their root causes and cost.
Assess whether resources (people, systems, spend) are deployed efficiently relative to workload and output across the four functions.
Evaluate whether SLAs/KPIs are defined, measured, reported and actively managed, and whether continuous-improvement mechanisms and process documentation are embedded.
Confirm that handoffs and dependencies between the functions (e.g. credit-to-finance, procurement-to-finance, risk-to-credit) are clear, timely and not a source of friction or duplication.
Identify quantified, actionable process-improvement opportunities that enhance efficiency without weakening control.
keyRisks: Excessive end-to-end cycle times (e.g. loan processing, PO-to-payment, financial close, risk reporting) reducing service quality, competitiveness and timely decision-making.
Heavy reliance on manual, spreadsheet-based and paper processes with low straight-through processing, increasing cost, error and key-person dependency.
Bottlenecks and unclear ownership at handoffs between Credit, Procurement, Finance and Risk causing delay, backlog and duplicated effort.
High rework, exception and error rates (e.g. rejected requisitions, mis-keyed loans, reconciliation differences, re-run risk reports) consuming capacity and inflating cost.
Duplication of activity and controls across functions (e.g. multiple re-keying of the same data, overlapping reconciliations and reports) adding cost without added assurance.
Absence or non-use of meaningful SLAs/KPIs and process metrics, so inefficiency and backlogs go unmeasured and unmanaged.
Sub-optimal resource utilisation — uneven workload distribution, overtime/backlogs in some teams and under-utilisation in others.
Inefficient or redundant controls that slow processing without commensurate risk reduction.
